what: After a sign-in with a one-time code, a person who already has a PIN is offered a new one without the old PIN. The offer is remembered on the device until it is answered, but the allowance to skip the old PIN ends 15 minutes after the code sign-in. Answering later than that gives "Type your current PIN first." on a box that has no current PIN field, so the save can never go through there.
expected: After the 15 minutes the box shows a current PIN field, or closes and says to sign in with a new code.

how_often: whenever the box is answered more than 15 minutes after the code sign-in

title: A staff member's job name can be typed only while adding the person and never changed after
what: The job (for example Manager) is typed in the Add a person form under Other. The person's row afterwards offers a sign-in code, sign out, the Trainer tick and Remove, but no way to change or clear the job. A typing mistake, a promotion, or a person added as plain Staff can only be fixed by removing the person and adding them again, which also signs them out.
expected: The owner can change or clear the job on the person's row at any time.

how_often: every time a job needs to change

title: Crash reports never say which page broke
what: When a page of the admin app breaks, the report sent to MettleUp is meant to carry the page it happened on. The app keeps its page in the part of the address after the # sign, but the report reads the part before it, which is always the same. Every report says the same page.
expected: The report names the page that broke (with ids taken out), so a crash can be found and fixed.
who: MettleUp team; owners and staff wait longer for a fix
how_often: every crash report
fix_line: Read the page from the part of the address after the # sign, with ids taken out

title: Front desk demo: the Member messages badge says 3 but only 2 messages wait
what: In the demo opened as the front desk, the menu badge and the Needs you count for Member messages include the complaint that the desk is not shown. The desk sees 3 on the badge and 2 cards under Waiting for a reply.
expected: The count shown to the front desk counts only the conversations the front desk can open, so the badge and the list agree.
who: prospects shown the front desk demo
how_often: every time
fix_line: Count only the conversations the signed-in demo person can see

title: Demo gym: two body measurements can be saved for the same day
what: In the demo gym, adding measurements for a member on a day that already has an entry adds a second entry for that day. The real gym refuses this, because a member has one entry per day.
expected: The demo turns away a second entry for the same day, as the real gym does, so the prospect sees the real rule.
who: prospects trying the demo gym
how_often: every time a second entry is added for one day
fix_line: Refuse a second entry for the same member and day in the demo, as the real gym does

title: Demo gym: an approved renewal or pause says only "Approved", without the new dates
what: In the demo gym, approving a member's renew or pause request on Today shows only "Approved by Vikram Rathore." The real gym shows the new plan dates and "Collect the fee at the desk.", which is the point of the demo.
expected: After Approve, the demo shows "Renewed by ...: <start> - <end>. Collect the fee at the desk." or "Paused by .... Plan now ends <date>.", as the real gym does.
who: prospects trying the demo gym
how_often: every approval
fix_line: Fill in the new start and end dates from the plan when the demo approves a request

title: A payment taken with no internet from the Dues list only says "Payment saved."
what: From a member's page, a payment taken with no internet says it is saved on this device, gives its receipt number and says it goes online later. The same payment taken from the Dues list in Money says only "Payment saved.", with no receipt number and no word that it is still only on this device.
expected: The Dues list gives the same message as the member page: saved on this device, the receipt number, and that it goes online when the internet is back.
who: owners and desk staff
how_often: every payment taken from the Dues list while the internet is off
fix_line: Use the member page's message, with the receipt number, on the Dues list too

title: The desk sees an empty "Pay online" box when the gym has no UPI ID
what: In a gym with no UPI ID and no payment company, a desk login that opens Collect payment or Sell membership sees a box headed "Pay online" with nothing in it. The owner sees a line telling them to add the UPI ID; the desk gets no words and no button.
expected: The box is hidden for the desk when there is nothing to offer, or says in one line that the owner can switch this on in Settings.
who: desk staff of gyms with no UPI ID saved
how_often: every time such a desk opens a money sheet for ₹1 or more
fix_line: Hide the box for the desk when there is no UPI ID and no payment company

title: The owner is told "The owner gives the extra days." when the member has no plan to add days to
what: After checking a workout code, the owner should get a "Give extra days" button. When the member has no gym plan that can take days (only a personal-training pack, or every plan cancelled), the owner instead reads "The owner gives the extra days.", the line meant for the desk, and has no button and no reason.
expected: The owner is told why no days can be given (the member has no plan to add them to) and what to do, such as sell or restore a plan first.
who: owners
how_often: each time a workout code is checked for a member with check-ins but no gym plan that is not cancelled
fix_line: Give the owner their own line that says the member needs a plan first

title: With "Comes with a pass" ticked and no company picked, "Add member" can look as if it does nothing
what: When the pass box is ticked and no company chip is picked, pressing Add member (or Save changes) saves nothing and writes "Pick or type the pass company." under the chips. Every other wrong box is scrolled into view, but this message is not, because the chips are not marked as a wrong box. The pass part sits near the top of a long form and the button is at the bottom, so on a phone the message is off the screen and the button seems dead.
expected: The pass company message is brought into view like every other wrong box, so the desk sees why nothing was saved.
who: owners and front-desk staff adding a pass member
how_often: each time the pass box is ticked, no company is picked and the form is scrolled down
fix_line: Scroll to the pass company message when it is the reason nothing was saved

title: The "price is more than the plan price" question stays on screen after another plan is picked
what: On the sell sheet, after the question about a high price or fee appears, picking another plan empties the price boxes but leaves the old question and the "Yes, save" button. The next tap saves the other plan at its normal price while the screen still talks about the old amount.
expected: Picking another plan removes the question and puts the button back to "Confirm", the same as editing the price does.
who: owners and front desk
how_often: only when the plan is changed after the question shows
fix_line: Clear the question whenever the plan is changed

title: Today's member news depends on the clock of the phone or laptop
what: Today lists member news of the last 24 hours and writes how long ago each came, by comparing the server's time with the clock of the device. On a device whose clock runs a day ahead, messages and requests that still need someone drop off Today; on a device that runs behind, old lines stay and say 'Just now'. The server's own clock comes with the list but is not used here.
expected: Today uses the server's clock for the 24 hour cut and for the age words, so a wrong device clock never hides a line that still needs someone.
who: owners, front desk and trainers on a device with a wrong clock
how_often: only on a device whose clock is wrong by hours
fix_line: Use the server's clock that comes with the list for the cut and the age words

title: The WhatsApp follow-up to a web-page enquiry carries the system note
what: For a person who asked on the gym web page or joined online, the ready WhatsApp message reads "you asked about <gym> (Asked on your web page: …)" or "(Joined online: …)". The enquiry card hides that note, the message does not.
expected: The message leaves out the system note, or uses only the words the person typed.
who: owners and front desk, and the people they message
how_often: every WhatsApp tap on an enquiry that came from the web page or online join

title: The growth Excel file shows a renewal rate the page hides
what: For a month whose 15 renewal days are not over, the page shows "–" for renewal rate and members lost, but the downloaded file gives a rate (often 100%) and a lost count made from the few plans decided so far.
expected: The file leaves the renewal rate and members lost empty for such a month, like the page.

how_often: every download, for the latest one or two months

title: Workout code check calls entry-machine check-ins "imported"
what: In the summary line of "Check workout code", every matched day that was not at the desk or in the app is counted as "imported". A check-in at the entry machine falls in that group, while the row below it says "Checked in at the entry machine".
expected: The summary names entry-machine check-ins as such, and "imported" only for imported ones.
who: owners and front desk at gyms with an entry machine
how_often: every code check for a member who enters by the machine

title: 'Download all your gym's data' leaves out much of the gym's data
what: The button and the help page say the file holds all the gym's data. The Excel file has eight sheets: about, members, plans, memberships, payments, check-ins, enquiries and expenses. Shop products and orders, diet plans, trainers and their bookings, staff, body measurements, member messages and photos are in neither file. Workout plans are only in the second, technical file.
expected: The download holds every kind of record the gym keeps in MettleUp, or the button and the help page name exactly what is inside and what is not.

how_often: every download

title: Times in the gym's data download are 5 and a half hours behind India time
what: The check-in time, the day the gym was set up, the download time and the time an enquiry was added are written in world time, not India time, and nothing in the file says so. A 6:00 am check-in reads 00:30, and one before 5:30 am shows the day before next to the right date. The file's name carries the world date too, so a download before 5:30 am is named for yesterday.
expected: Every time and the file name use India time, the same as the panel's own screens.
who: owners
how_often: every download
fix_line: Write the times and the file date in India time

title: 'Your questions' in Help shows one person's questions to the next person on the same computer
what: The list of questions, AI answers and replies from MettleUp is kept in the browser, not per person or per gym, and signing out does not clear it. On a shared desk computer the staff see what the owner asked and what MettleUp replied. The owner's 'delete our gym' request, with the gym's name, code and phone, lands in the same list. expected: Each person sees only the questions they sent; the list is tied to the gym and the signed-in person and is cleared or hidden at sign-out.

title: Import button says 'Update 1 members'
what: When exactly one member already in the gym gets blank details filled in and nobody new is added, the import button reads 'Update 1 members'.
expected: 'Update 1 member', the same way the button says 'Add 1 member'.

how_often: each import that updates exactly one member
fix_line: Use the singular for one, as the add label does

title: A special day with a past date vanishes without a word
what: On Gym timings, a special day whose date is already over (for example a wrong year) is dropped before the check and before the comparison with the saved timings. expected: The owner is told the date is over, or the date box refuses a past day.

how_often: when a special day is typed with a past date

title: An imported plan named like '3 days a week' becomes a 3-day plan
what: When another software's sheet names a plan by how often the member comes, such as '3 Days a Week Monthly' or '5 days/week 3 months', the import reads the first number and word as the plan's length. The new plan is saved as 3 (or 5) days long, and a row with a start date but no end date gets a membership that ends after 3 days and shows as expired.
expected: A number followed by 'days a week', 'days/week' or 'per week' is not a length; the month or year word in the name (or the row's own dates) decides it.

how_often: every import with such plan names
fix_line: Skip a number that counts days per week when reading a plan's length from its name

title: Past pass visits change when a pass member is edited
what: A check-in the member made by scanning the gym's QR carries no pass company of its own; the panel works it out from the member as they are today. Untick the pass box and every past QR visit of that member leaves the monthly count; tick it again and the first day becomes today, so the old visits stay lost; change the company and the old QR visits move to the new company. The gym then claims too little (or from the wrong company) for a month it has not been paid for yet.
expected: A visit that counted for a pass company on the day it happened keeps counting for that company, whatever is changed on the member later.

how_often: each time a pass member stops, restarts or changes company before the month is matched

title: A second friend with the same name gets the member a "Free days added" message but no days
what: When a member brings two friends who have exactly the same name, the thank-you for the second friend adds nothing to the member's plan. The screen still says the free days were added and gives a new last day, and the friend is marked as rewarded, so the offer never comes back.

how_often: rare: one member brings two friends with the same name

title: In the quick buttons sheet the up and down arrows move nothing the owner can see in the list

title: A workout offer with a 1-day reward says "Give 1 days" and "1 days added"

title: A second friend with the same name earns the member no free days, yet the screen says they were added

expected: Each friend who joins gives the member the free days once; the already-given check should look at this friend’s own enquiry, not at the friend’s name.

title: Gym timings says 'Right now members see' for times that are not saved yet

title: An owner checking a workout code is told "The owner gives the extra days." when the member has no gym plan to add days to
what: After a good workout code, the owner normally gets a "Give extra days" button. If the member has no gym plan that is not cancelled (for example only a personal training pack, or a cancelled plan), the button is left out and the owner reads "The owner gives the extra days.", the line meant for front desk staff. how_often: each time a workout code is checked for a member with no gym plan that can take days

title: A MettleUp receipt that fails to load says "Receipt not found"
what: When the owner opens a receipt for a payment to MettleUp and the internet is off or the server does not answer, the page says "Receipt not found. title: A receipt number that is not sure yet can still be sent to the member on WhatsApp

title: On a trainer's page showing a past week, the booking sheet offers only a day that is already over

title: 'Copy link' on the web page says nothing when the copy fails

title: Web page editor says '1 plans from Plans'

title: Join link cards say people pay at the desk even when paying online is on

title: A real gym owner is told their demo gym is gone

title: All branches tells an owner who cannot open other branches that the gym has one branch

title: Quick buttons the owner picks stay on his own device

title: Drive sign-in message names two buttons that do not exist

expected: The owner's words say plainly that MettleUp can also open access in an emergency, as the privacy page does, or the emergency door asks the owner.
who: gym owners
how_often: every time an owner reads the card
fix_line: Add the emergency door to the owner's words on both screens

title: Wrong tries when changing a PIN lock it for only 15 minutes every time
what: Since the November security fix, wrong PINs on the sign-in page lock for longer each time in a day (15 minutes, then 1 hour). Wrong current PINs typed while changing the PIN in Settings still lock for a fixed 15 minutes and do not count toward the longer lock.
expected: Wrong current PINs in Settings count toward the same growing lock as the sign-in page.
who: owners and desk staff
how_often: every time someone guesses the current PIN while changing it
fix_line: Use the same growing lock when changing a PIN

title: A leaderboard update sent within 15 seconds of the last one is thrown away, even with new workouts
what: When a phone sends its day totals less than 15 seconds after its last send, with the name switch unchanged, the server answers OK and keeps nothing, even if a new workout was added. The design note says only a send that changes nothing should be ignored. The owner hiding a member also restarts the 15 seconds.
expected: A send with new numbers is always kept; only an identical send inside 15 seconds is skipped.
who: members
how_often: when two sends come close together, for example on opening the app right after a workout
fix_line: Skip only when the days sent are the same as the ones kept

title: A member's progress summary is stored again after they leave the gym
what: When a member leaves, their trainer summary is deleted at once. But the three ways the phone sends a summary never check whether the member has left, so the next send from an app that still has sharing on stores the summary again. Nobody at the gym can see it (the lists skip members who left), but it stays on the server until a trainer list is read 90 days later, against the privacy notice's promise that it is deleted on leaving. The gym mate sharing, by contrast, refuses a member who left.
expected: A send from a member who left is refused, and nothing is stored.
who: members who leave a gym with sharing still on
how_often: every time such an app sends after leaving
fix_line: Refuse the summary send for a member who has left, as the gym mate sharing does

title: In a paused gym a member cannot take back a request or clear an answer
what: While the gym is paused, the guard on the pause and renew requests also blocks deleting and updating them. Taking back a waiting request or marking an answer as seen then fails with an error, though the member side promises never to raise an error after the key check, and the other new tables allow deleting in a paused gym.
expected: Taking back a request and marking an answer as seen keep working in a paused gym; only new requests and decisions stop.
who: members of a paused gym
how_often: only while a gym is paused
fix_line: Let the pause guard allow deletes and the seen mark

title: The nightly backup can catch a payment without its receipt, though it says it never can
what: The nightly copy reads each table one after another inside a function marked as changing data. In the normal database mode such a function sees fresh data at every read, so a payment saved while the copy runs can be in one table of the copy and missing from the other. The file says every table is read at one moment.
expected: All tables in one copy are read at the same moment, so a restore never has a payment without its receipt.
who: HQ
how_often: rare: only when someone saves while the nightly copy runs
fix_line: Read all the tables in one read-only helper that sees a single moment, then write the audit line

title: What's new tells owners members get a pop-up when the gym sends a report they asked for, but the pop-up is for the gym asking
what: The admin app's What's new line says members get a notification when the gym sends the workout report they asked for. The server only makes a pop-up when the gym asks a member for their report; nothing pops up when a report is sent.
expected: The What's new line says members get a pop-up when the gym asks for their workout report.
who: owners
how_often: every time
fix_line: Change the What's new line to say the pop-up comes when the gym asks for the report

title: A real gym named "QA ..." is deleted overnight
what: The nightly clean-up of test gyms picks gyms only by name: any gym whose name starts with capital QA and a space, more than a day old, is deleted with all its members and money records. Nothing stops a real owner from naming a gym that way.
expected: Only gyms made by the phone tests are deleted, marked as test gyms when they are made; a real gym is never picked by its name.
who: owners
how_often: rare: only a gym whose name starts with QA and a space
fix_line: Mark test gyms when they are made and delete only marked ones

title: AI credits can be given back for a task that worked
what: The give-back of AI credits accepts any spend from the last 10 minutes and marks the task failed; it never checks that the task really failed. An owner key calling it directly gets every task free.
expected: Credits come back only for a task that did not finish.
who: MettleUp (credit income)
how_often: only when someone calls the server directly
fix_line: Refuse a give-back unless the task is still waiting or recorded as failed

title: The HQ Log records a feedback or lead change even when it was refused
what: When HQ saves a status on a feedback message or a lead, the Log line is written first. If the message or lead is gone, or the status is not one of the allowed ones, the change is refused but the Log still says it was made.
expected: The Log gets a line only when the change was really saved.
who: MettleUp HQ
how_often: every refused feedback or lead save
fix_line: Write the Log line after the save, only when it changed a row

title: A lead sent from the member app shows an empty call link and no word where it came from
what: The member app's 'Tell my gym' sends a lead with only the gym's name and city, no mobile. The Leads page still draws the mobile as a call link (empty) and only names leads from a member's shared link, so HQ cannot tell who to call or why the number is missing.
expected: The card says the lead came from a member in the app, has no number, and how to reach the gym.
who: MettleUp HQ
how_often: every lead sent from the member app's Tell my gym
fix_line: Label member-app leads and hide the call link when there is no number

title: Deleting a gym leaves the photos of its web page behind
what: When HQ deletes a whole gym, only the gym logo and the shop product photos are collected for removal. The photos the owner put on the gym web page stay in storage, and the success note still says the pictures were removed.
expected: Every file of the gym, its web page photos too, is removed, or the note lists what is left to remove by hand.
who: gyms that leave MettleUp after putting photos on their web page
how_often: every gym delete of a gym that had web page photos
fix_line: Also collect and remove the gym web page photos when a gym is deleted

title: MettleUp can open a gym's records without the gym saying yes, while the app promises it never does
what: HQ has an "Open in an emergency" button that opens read access to a gym's members, payments and staff without the gym asking. The gym owner's own screen and the pilot agreement say MettleUp support can look only when the gym lets them.
expected: Either the emergency opening is removed, or every promise says MettleUp may open it in an emergency and the owner is told with the reason.
who: gym owners and their members
how_often: every time HQ uses the emergency button
fix_line: Make the promise and the emergency button say the same thing

title: An empty daily limit box switches the gym's AI Assistant off
what: On a gym's HQ page, clearing "AI requests a day" or "Spoken minutes a day" and tapping "Save the limit" sends 0, which switches the AI Assistant off for that gym. The server would treat an empty box as the normal limit, but the page never sends it empty.
expected: An empty box keeps the normal limit, or the page asks for a number.
who: gym owners (through an HQ slip)
how_often: when HQ saves with a box left empty
fix_line: Send an empty box as empty, not as 0

title: A member checking their number in the app is told to go back to a "page" when the message has no code
what: When a member who started "Find my gym by my number" in the member app sends a WhatsApp message without the code, MettleUp replies "Go back to the MettleUp page, tap Open WhatsApp again". The member is in the app, not on a page. The success reply already says "app" for these members; the no-code reply does not.
expected: A member who started in the app is told to go back to the MettleUp app.
who: members
how_often: every time a member app check gets a message with no right code
fix_line: Give the no-code reply an app version, as the success reply has

title: Heart rate keeps the last number after the watch leaves the wrist
what: When the watch is taken off the wrist (or the sensor stops giving readings) with the screen on, the heart line keeps showing the last number, such as 132, as if it were live. The watch knows it is off the wrist but never shows it.
expected: The number goes to a dash, or a short word says the watch is off the wrist.
who: members with a watch
how_often: rarely: only with the watch off the wrist and the screen on mid-workout
fix_line: Clear the number when the watch says it is off the wrist or unavailable

title: A rest that ends seconds before a watch restart is left hanging
what: If a rest ends in the five seconds before the watch finishes restarting or the app finishes updating, the rest is neither set again nor cleared: no buzz, no card, and it stays saved as running until the app is opened or the phone sends something.
expected: A rest that ended moments ago either buzzes once (as a late phone message does) or is cleared.
who: members with a watch
how_often: rarely: a restart or update must end within seconds of a rest's end
fix_line: Treat a just-ended rest at start-up as over: buzz once or clear it

title: The check for full-size watch numbers cannot catch the bug it was written for
what: The automatic check that the watch countdown keeps its size at the largest text feeds the text size in the simple old way, so the newer Android scaling that made the numbers 23 % smaller is never tried. The old broken code would also pass it, so a return of the bug would not be noticed before release.
expected: The check runs with the real newer Android text scaling (or a watch on Wear OS 5), so the old shrinking code would fail it.
who: members
how_often: only if the size bug comes back
fix_line: Run the size check with the real Android text scaling instead of a simple multiplier

title: The invite page always says "You pay at the gym desk", even when the gym takes join payments online
what: The "Not a member yet?" card on a gym's invite link page always says the person pays at the gym desk. The link preview was changed to drop that sentence once online join payments are on, because the gym may then take the money online, but the card itself was not.
expected: The card says nothing about how to pay, or says the right way for this gym, like the link preview does.
who: people invited to a gym that takes online join payments
how_often: every visit once join payments are on
fix_line: Drop the pay sentence from the card, or fill it the same way as the preview

title: The daily limits on feedback, bring-a-friend and online join restart every morning at 05:30, not 24 hours later
what: The limit per internet address is meant to count the last 24 hours, but the coded address changes every day at 05:30 India time. Sends from before 05:30 are no longer seen, so one address can send up to twice the limit around that time.
expected: The limit counts every send from that address in the last 24 hours, or is stated as a per-day limit that resets at a fixed time.
who: everyone sending a form or feedback
how_often: every day around 05:30 India time
fix_line: Count by the same day the coded address uses, or keep the coded address the same for 24 hours

title: No test proves an owner's AI usage numbers leave out another gym's questions
what: The AI credits sheet shows who asked the AI this month (owner, staff, members, page visitors) and the gym's question slots. The database tests check these numbers only while no other gym has any questions logged, so nothing would catch a change that started counting another gym's questions. The code keeps gyms apart today.
expected: A database test logs questions for a second gym and shows the first owner's numbers stay the same.
who: owners
how_often: only if a future change breaks the gym filter
fix_line: Add a second gym with logged questions to the AI questions test and check the first owner's numbers do not move

title: A gym panel sign-in never runs out
what: Once a person signs in to the gym panel on a browser, that sign-in stays good for ever: it has no end date and no idle limit. It ends only when someone taps Sign out on that device, an owner signs that person out everywhere, the person is removed, or the person signs in on more than 10 other devices. A desk computer that is sold, a shared laptop, or a copied browser profile keeps full access to the gym's members, money and records with no time limit if nobody remembers to sign it out.
expected: A sign-in that has not been used for a while (for example 30 to 90 days) stops working by itself and asks for the PIN again, so a forgotten device does not keep the gym open for ever.
who: gym owners and their desk staff
how_often: only when a signed-in device is lost, sold or shared and not signed out
fix_line: Refuse a panel sign-in that has not been seen for a set number of days, and ask for the PIN again

title: A stranger can list your mobile in their own gym, and Forgot PIN then opens their gym too
what: Any owner can add any mobile number to their gym's staff list, and while the number check is switched off anyone can also make a new gym with any mobile as its owner. The number's real holder is never asked. When that person later uses Forgot PIN, the new PIN is set on every gym where the number is listed, including the stranger's. At sign-in, when two gyms share the number and the PIN, the panel opens the one whose device was used most recently, so the stranger's gym can open instead of the person's own, and anything they then type (members, payments) lands in the stranger's gym. A number made into a gym owner this way also loses its free trial later.
expected: A number only joins a gym's sign-in list once its holder has confirmed it, and Forgot PIN or sign-in never opens a gym the person did not choose (ask which gym when there is more than one).
who: gym owners and desk staff whose number is listed by someone else
how_often: only if someone deliberately lists another person's number
fix_line: Ask which gym to open when a number is in more than one, and let Forgot PIN reset only gyms the person picks

title: No test proves another gym's owner cannot see this gym's support-access record or terms record
what: The database tests check that a bad key is refused for the MettleUp-access screen and the terms screen, but no test signs in as a second gym's owner and checks that they see none of the first gym's support-access windows, what support looked at, or who accepted the terms. The test named for the other gym actually uses a made-up key, and the second gym's owner key it prepares is never used. The code takes the gym from the key, so it looks safe today, but nothing would catch a change that broke it.
expected: A test signs in as gym B's owner and shows that gym A's support-access windows, looks and terms acceptance never appear.
who: gym owners
how_often: only if a future change breaks the gym check
fix_line: Add gym B owner checks to the support-access and terms database tests

title: A gym owner can show another gym's logo as their own, and no test checks it
what: When an owner saves the gym's look, the server only checks that the logo sits in the shared logo store. It does not check that the logo was uploaded by this gym, so an owner can point their member app at another gym's logo. The database tests try only a made-up upload ticket; none tries a second gym. Gym web page photos already have this check and a test.
expected: A gym can only use a logo it uploaded itself, and a test proves another gym's logo is refused.
who: owners
how_often: only if an owner copies another gym's logo link
fix_line: Remember which gym each upload ticket belongs to and accept only that gym's logos; add a second-gym test

title: Anyone with a member app account can create any number of empty gyms
what: An old gym-creation step from the first version of the admin app is still switched on for every signed-in account. The admin app no longer uses it (that screen is kept on disk only), but any member app account can still call it as often as it likes, with no limit and no name check. Each call also turns that account into the owner of the new empty gym, taking it out of its real gym.
expected: Gyms are created only through today's sign-up and HQ paths, with their limits; the old step is switched off.
who: everyone
how_often: only if someone calls it on purpose
fix_line: Take the old create-gym step away from signed-in accounts, or remove it

title: No test proves another gym's owner cannot read this gym's member sign-in profiles
what: The read rule on member sign-in profiles lets a gym's owner or trainer read the profiles of their own gym. The access test checks that a member cannot raise their own role, but never tries an owner of a second gym reading the first gym's profiles. The workout summaries next to it do have that test.
expected: A test signs in as another gym's owner and proves no profile of this gym comes back.
who: members
how_often: no known case; a gap in the safety net
fix_line: Add one row to the access test: another gym's owner reads this gym's profiles and gets none

title: A front-desk login can switch on "train at every branch" for a member, although only the owner is meant to
what: On the add or edit member form, the "train at every branch" choice is shown to the owner only. But the server takes any change to a member from a front-desk login without looking at that choice, so a desk login that sends the change outside the panel's own screens can let a member check in at every branch. The panel's own notes say the server enforces the desk's limits on writes; this one is missing.
expected: The server refuses a front-desk change that turns "train at every branch" on or off, the same way it refuses desk changes to plans, receipts and memberships, and a database test proves it.
who: owners with two or more branches
how_often: only when someone at the desk sends the change outside the panel's screens
fix_line: Make the server refuse a desk login's change to the every-branch choice, and add a test for it

title: No test proves another business cannot see or take back a visitor check-in at a branch
what: A desk can check in a member of another branch of the same business, list today's visitors from other branches, and take a visit back. The server checks that the other branch belongs to the same business, and a test proves another business is refused when it looks up a mobile number or checks someone in. But no test sends another business's key to the visitors list or to taking a visit back, and no test reads the business and look-up tables directly as an app user while they hold rows. Today the checks are correct; a later change could drop one with no test failing.
expected: Every branch call that touches another branch's members has a test that sends a key of an unrelated business and expects a refusal or nothing.
who: gyms with more than one branch
how_often: only if a later change breaks the check
fix_line: Add refusal tests with an unrelated business's key for the visitors list and for taking a visit back

title: No test proves another gym is refused on busy machines, Bring a friend counts, the leaderboard owner view, the challenge reward confirm, or the entry machine screens
what: Each of these owner calls works out the gym from the sign-in key and only touches that gym's rows, so reading the code found no leak. But the database tests never try them with a second gym's key. The busy machines test makes a second gym's owner key and never uses it; the Bring a friend counts are only asked by the gym's own owner; the leaderboard owner view and the challenge reward confirm are only tested on each gym's own records. The five entry machine owner calls (add or remove a machine, give a member a machine number, send machine orders, the list) are live on the server and have no test of their own at all, only the line saying they may be called without signing in. A later change that drops the gym check would still pass the build.
expected: For every owner call this area uses, a database test tries it with another gym's owner key and proves it sees, changes and removes nothing of the first gym.
who: gym owners and their members
how_often: no harm today; only if a later change breaks the gym check
fix_line: Add a second-gym check to the busy machines, Bring a friend, leaderboard and reward tests, and write a test file for the entry machine owner calls before that feature goes live

title: Disconnect the shop forgets the gym's owner key in this browser only; the key keeps working on the server
what: In Settings, a gym that turned the shop on but is not online yet can press Disconnect the shop. The browser forgets the gym's owner key, but nothing tells the server, so the key stays live. Anyone who copied it earlier (a shared desk computer, an old browser) keeps full owner powers: member messages, the web page, payments to MettleUp. The button even says it needs the internet, yet it sends nothing.
expected: Disconnecting retires the key on the server too (the server already has a way to retire the old owner key), so a forgotten key cannot be used again.
who: owners
how_often: rare
fix_line: On Disconnect, ask the server to retire the key before forgetting it, and say so if it fails

title: A front-desk login can give any member door access with any end date, paid or not
what: When entry machines are on, the admin app works out each member's door dates from their plan and sends them to the server to pass on to the door machines. The server accepts these orders from any front-desk login and checks only that the member number belongs to the gym. It never checks the dates against the member's real plan. A desk login that sends its own order (for example from the browser's developer tools) can switch a lapsed member on, or give them no end date at all. The server already stops the desk from handing out free months in the member records, so this is a way round that rule.
expected: The server works out a member's door dates from the saved plan itself, or refuses a desk order whose dates go beyond the member's paid plan.
who: owners
how_often: only if a desk login sends its own order; entry machines are behind a switch
fix_line: Let the server set door dates from the saved plan instead of taking them from the browser

title: No test proves another gym is refused when editing, hiding or re-photographing a product, reading the app members list, or saving alert settings
what: Each of these calls works out the gym from the sign-in key and only touches that gym's rows, so reading the code found no leak. But the database tests never try them with a second gym's key. The access test table covers listing, restocking and deleting a product, not editing, hiding or changing its photo. The app members list (names and mobile numbers of members who joined from the app) has no test of its own at all, only a line saying it may be called without signing in. Alert settings are tested with this gym's owner and desk only, though a second gym's key is made in the same test. A later change that broke the gym check would not be caught.
expected: For each of these calls, a database test uses a second gym's owner key against the first gym's product, members and settings and checks that it is refused or sees nothing.
who: owners
how_often: only if a later change breaks the gym check
fix_line: Add second-gym refusal checks for these calls to the database tests

title: The workout import reads files with an old spreadsheet library that has two known high-rated flaws
what: Bring in past workouts reads a Hevy or Strong export picked by the member, or a file shared into the app from another app such as WhatsApp, with spreadsheet library version 0.18.5. That version has two high-rated known flaws: a crafted file can change how the app's own objects behave, or make the reading freeze. The library's npm copy will never get a fix; the web panel already moved to the maker's fixed build (0.20.3).
expected: The phone app reads spreadsheet files with a version past both fixes (0.20.2 or newer), as the panel already does.
who: members
how_often: only when a crafted file is imported
fix_line: Switch the phone app to the spreadsheet maker's own fixed build, as the panel did

title: No test proves another gym's member cannot send a workout report, add workout dates, or leave a workout offer for this gym
what: Three member calls take an id that belongs to the gym: sending the workout report the desk asked for, adding workout dates to the gym's offer, and leaving the offer. Reading the server code, each one only acts on a record of the member's own gym (and own person), so no leak was found. But the database tests only ever call these three with the member's own key and own gym's ids; none tries another gym's member, unlike the other member calls (plan requests, questions, messages, mate profiles, check-in), which do have such a test. A later change could drop the gym check without any test failing.
expected: Each of the three has a database test where a member of another gym (and another member of the same gym) names this gym's request or offer and is refused.
who: members and gym owners
how_often: no known trigger today; only if a later change breaks the check
fix_line: Add a refusal test for another gym's member on each of the three calls

title: The phone app reads Hevy and Strong export files with a spreadsheet library that has two known serious flaws
what: When a member brings in workouts from Hevy or Strong, the phone opens the file they picked with spreadsheet library version 0.18.5. The dependency scan marks two high-severity flaws in that version: one lets a crafted file tamper with the app's internal objects, the other lets a crafted file freeze the reader. There is no fixed version on the public package registry, so the scan offers no automatic upgrade. The risk is limited because the member picks their own file.
expected: The importer uses a spreadsheet reader with no known high-severity flaws, as the gym panel already does with its newer copy.
who: members who import workouts from Hevy or Strong
how_often: only when a member imports a crafted file
fix_line: Move the phone app to the spreadsheet library's own newer release (the one the gym panel already uses), then re-run the import tests.

title: The phone app's screen-navigation library is flagged high by the dependency scan
what: The library that moves the phone app between screens is marked high severity by the dependency scan, through a link-reading package it pulls in. The scan says the fix needs a major upgrade of that library. Every screen in this area uses it, including the gym's workout of the day and the import card.
expected: The navigation library has no high-severity alerts, or the alert is checked and written down as not reachable in this app.
who: all phone app members
how_often: unknown; depends on whether a crafted link can reach it
fix_line: Check whether the flagged link-reading path is reachable; if it is, plan the major navigation upgrade with the next app dependency bump.

title: The library the phone uses to hand a picture or file to other apps is flagged by the dependency scan
what: Sharing a workout picture or a routine file goes through the phone's sharing library. The dependency scan marks the installed version as a moderate risk, through a build-time setup package it pulls in. The scan says the fix is a major upgrade of that library. Nothing has written down whether the flagged part ever runs on a member's phone.
expected: The sharing library has no open alerts, or the alert is checked and written down as build-time only and not reachable on the phone.
who: members who share a workout picture or a routine
how_often: unknown; the flagged part looks build-time only
fix_line: Confirm the flagged part only runs while building the app; move to the newer sharing library with the next Expo upgrade.

title: Save my history writes workout and exercise names into the spreadsheet file exactly as typed, so a name starting with = runs as a formula
what: Save my history puts each workout name, workout note, exercise name and exercise note into the spreadsheet file inside quotes, but does not neutralise text that starts with =, +, - or @. When the member opens that file in Excel or Google Sheets, such a cell is treated as a formula. Most of this text is the member's own, but exercise names also arrive from the gym's workout plans and from shared routine files, which create new exercises under whatever name the sender chose. A crafted name could show a misleading link or pull data into the sheet when opened.
expected: Any text cell that starts with =, +, - or @ is written so a spreadsheet shows it as plain text, while the file still imports back into Hevy, Strong and MettleUp.
who: members who save their history and open it in a spreadsheet app
how_often: only when a workout or exercise name starts with a formula sign
fix_line: Prefix text cells that start with a formula sign with a single quote when writing the file, and teach the importer to drop that quote.

title: Outside code is fetched fresh, by a moving version, right next to MettleUp's most powerful keys
what: Several cloud jobs run code from other people that is fetched by a moving name, not a fixed copy. The release job hands a third-party publishing tool the right to write to the code store; the WhatsApp set-up job downloads the newest Cloudflare tool while holding the Cloudflare edit key and the WhatsApp key; the phone test jobs pipe an installer script from the internet straight into the shell. The code host settings do not demand fixed copies, and the main branch has no protection. If any of those outside sources is taken over, it could read the keys or change the code the next release is built from.
expected: Every outside action and tool that runs next to a key is locked to one checked copy, and the job that only publishes holds no wider rights than it needs.
who: every member and gym, if a supplier is hacked
how_often: only if an outside supplier is taken over
fix_line: Lock outside actions and tools to fixed versions and turn on the setting that requires it

title: Nothing warns about known security holes in the libraries the apps use
what: The code host's automatic security alerts are switched off, and no cloud check looks for libraries with known holes. A one-off scan on 20 Nov 2026 found 3 critical and 49 high warnings. Most sit in build and test tools, not in what members run, but nobody would hear about a new one that does.
expected: A cloud check or the code host's alerts flag a library with a known hole, at least weekly.
who: the owner
how_often: all the time
fix_line: Turn on the code host's security alerts, or add a weekly library check to the cloud checks

title: The WhatsApp set-up run writes business account details into a log anyone can read
what: The code store is public, so every cloud run log is public. The WhatsApp set-up run prints the WhatsApp account's payment method id, currency, review state and business verification state into that log. No key is printed, but these are private business details.
expected: Public run logs show only pass or fail and the names of what was checked, not account billing details.
who: the owner
how_often: every time the set-up run is started
fix_line: Drop the payment and verification fields from what the set-up run prints

title: A gym's join code can be found by trying codes, and then anyone can join that gym's member app
what: A gym's join code is 6 characters made only of 0-9 and A-F, about 16.7 million possibilities. The public 'which gym is this code' check answers any code, with no limit on how many tries one caller makes. A script that tries codes finds real gyms and gets their name and logo; with the code it can then join the gym as an app member under any name and read the gym's messages, offers and shop.
expected: Codes that cannot be found by trying: a limit on wrong codes per caller, or longer codes, so only people who saw the code at the gym can use it.
who: owners and members
how_often: only when someone runs a script
fix_line: Count wrong codes per caller and stop after a few, or make new codes longer

title: Anyone can store any number of pictures on our server for free through a demo gym
what: 'Start demo' hands an owner key to anyone, with no sign-up. That key gets photo upload tickets, up to 50 at once. A ticket is not used up by an upload: for 15 minutes it lets in any number of files of up to 3 MB into a public picture store, and only the declared file type is checked. Files that no product or logo points at are never deleted. So a stranger can use our picture store as free public hosting, and we pay for the space.
expected: One upload per ticket (or a small number), and unused uploads cleaned away, so the picture store only holds pictures gyms really use.
who: the business (storage cost)
how_often: only when someone abuses it
fix_line: Make a ticket good for one file and delete pictures nothing points at

title: One person can block 'Start demo' for everyone, or block a gym's members from joining, for an hour
what: 'Start demo' stops after 300 demo gyms in an hour counted over all callers together, with no limit per caller, so one script can make 300 gyms and every real visitor then gets 'busy' for the rest of the hour. Joining a gym stops after 500 joins in an hour per gym, so anyone who has a gym's code can use that up and real members cannot join for an hour. The old 'create gym' for signed-in app users has no limit at all.
expected: Limits counted per caller, so one person cannot use up a shared allowance and lock out everybody else.
who: new owners trying the demo, members joining
how_often: only when someone abuses it
fix_line: Add a per-caller limit before the shared one, and cap or retire the old create gym

title: The nightly backup copies the WhatsApp number-check secret and every PIN fingerprint into a plain store for 7 days
what: The nightly backup copies every table of the gym server as it is. It carefully leaves out the passwords of sign-in accounts, but it does not leave out the server's own secrets: the secret that proves a mobile number was checked by WhatsApp (once that row is set live), every owner and desk PIN fingerprint, and the one-time code and sign-in key fingerprints. The copy sits unencrypted in the HQ Worker's Cloudflare store for 7 days and can be turned into a file on a laptop for a restore. Anyone who gets that copy can make their own 'number checked' proof for any mobile, reset that person's PIN and walk into their gym, and can try all one million PINs offline with no lock.
expected: A backup leaves out, or locks with a separate key, every secret it does not need to bring a gym back: the number-check secret, PIN fingerprints and one-time code fingerprints, the same way it already leaves out account passwords.
who: every gym owner and desk person
how_often: only if the backup store or a restore file is seen by the wrong person
fix_line: Leave the number-check secret and the PIN and code fingerprints out of the nightly copy (or lock the copy with its own key), and test that they are absent

title: Anyone can send a question from a gym's web page in another person's name and mobile number
what: The 'Ask the gym' form on a gym's web page takes a typed name and a typed mobile number and never checks that the number belongs to the sender (the Join online form does check, with WhatsApp). The question lands in the gym's Enquiries under that number, and if that number already has an open enquiry the new question and name are added to the real person's enquiry. The gym then calls or messages a person who never asked anything. The form can also be sent straight to the gym server, skipping the 5-a-day limit per network address, and 40 questions in a day from anyone close the form for every real visitor of that gym until the next day.
expected: A web page question is kept only after the sender proves the number (the same WhatsApp check Join online uses), or it is marked 'number not checked' and never added to someone's existing enquiry; the gym's daily limit cannot be used up by one sender.
who: gym owners and any person whose number is typed in
how_often: whenever someone types a number that is not theirs
fix_line: Ask for the WhatsApp number check before a web page question is kept, or keep unchecked questions apart and never merge them into an existing enquiry

title: Anyone with the public app key can list every gym's web page photos, unpublished drafts included
what: The photo store's read rule lets a file be read while it is on a gym's page row, published or not. The store's 'list' call uses the same rule, so anyone holding the public app key (it is inside every app) can list the photos of every gym that has a page, including pages the owner has not published yet, and each file's folder name is that gym's internal id. The file itself notes this as a known limit.
expected: Photos of a page that is not published can be seen only by that gym's own people; the public can list nothing and can open only photos of published pages.
who: gym owners preparing a web page
how_often: any time, by anyone who tries
fix_line: Let the public read only photos of published pages, and show unpublished drafts to the owner through a signed link

title: Reads of gym data made with the server's master app key are never recorded
what: The new direct-read record writes down every look at gym data made with the database owner login, and owners are told every look is recorded. Looks made with the server's master app key (the key the HQ and panel Workers use, which anyone with the Supabase dashboard can copy) are left out on purpose, so a person who copies that key can read every gym's members and money through the normal web address with no record at all.
expected: Every look at a gym's data that is not the app itself serving that gym is recorded, including looks made with the master app key outside the Workers; or that key is kept where no person can copy it and the promise says so.
who: every gym owner
how_often: only if a person reads data with the master app key
fix_line: Record reads made with the master app key that do not come from the Workers (for example by giving the Workers their own key), or change the promise to say what is not recorded

title: No test proves another gym cannot cancel this gym's personal-training booking, edit its trainer page, or turn off its browser alerts
what: The code limits each of these to the caller's own gym, but the database tests try another gym only for the week schedule and for booking with this gym's trainer. Nobody tests another gym's key cancelling a booking by its id, saving a trainer page for this gym's trainer, or removing this gym's saved browser for alerts. A later change could open them and every test would still pass.
expected: Each call that takes a booking, a person or a browser address has a test where another gym's key is refused and the row is unchanged.
who: gym owners and trainers
how_often: only if a later change breaks the gym check
fix_line: Add three refusals with the other gym's key to the trainer schedule and browser alert tests

title: Anyone who knows an entry machine's serial number can pose as that machine
what: The entry machine address takes no password. It trusts the serial number alone, and that number is printed on the machine and travels in plain view over unencrypted web calls. Anyone who has it can send made-up entries for that gym's members, collect the machine's waiting orders (these carry member names and numbers) and so stop the real machine from getting them, for example an order to remove a member whose plan ran out. Not live today: the entry machine service is written but not switched on.
expected: A machine should prove it is the gym's own machine with something only the gym set up, not a number printed on its label, before its entries are saved or member names are handed to it.
who: gyms and members, once entry machines go live
how_often: whenever someone learns a serial number
fix_line: Before going live, tie each machine to something the gym sets up (the machine's comm key or its fixed internet address), and keep member names out of the machine's orders where the machine does not need them

title: An HQ sign-in lasts 30 days and cannot be ended from another device
what: HQ keeps the owner signed in for 30 days with a sealed cookie that the server does not track. Sign out only wipes the cookie in the browser where it is tapped. If a phone or laptop with HQ open is lost, or the cookie is copied, it keeps full HQ access (every gym, payments, messages to every gym) for up to 30 days, and there is no 'sign out everywhere'. The only way to end it is to change a server secret by hand.
expected: The owner can end every HQ sign-in at once (for example from HQ itself), and a lost device stops working without a server change.
who: the owner
how_often: only if a device or its cookie is lost
fix_line: Store a sign-in version on the server and check it on each request, with a 'sign out everywhere' button that bumps it

title: Anyone on the internet can make HQ run its phone pop-up job
what: The address that makes HQ send due pop-ups needs no sign-in. Its 3-second brake is kept per server copy, not across all copies, so a flood of calls starts many runs. Each run only sends what is already due, so no extra pop-ups reach members, but every run spends gym-server calls and Cloudflare free-plan allowance.
expected: Only the gym admin app's own service (which already calls through a private link) can start the job early.
who: the owner (free-plan allowance)
how_often: only under deliberate abuse
fix_line: Accept the early-run call only through the private service link, or with a shared secret header

title: The database test that says no app can read a table checks HQ and entry machine tables while they are empty
what: The safety test reads every table as a visitor and as a signed-in app user and fails only if it gets rows back. It fills in only gyms, keys, one member and two records first. The delete requests list, the support access grants and the five entry machine tables are empty when it reads them, so the test would still pass if one of them were opened to the apps by mistake. Today they are closed (row rules on, no rule lets anyone in), but no test proves it with data present; the support grants test checks visitors only, not signed-in users.
expected: For each table that holds gym or person data, a test puts a row in and proves that a visitor, a signed-in user of no gym, and another gym's owner all get nothing.
who: every gym, if a table is ever opened by mistake
how_often: only after a wrong change
fix_line: Seed one row in every table before the read-everything check, or add a row per table to that check

title: Through our own server address every person looks like the same sender, so sign-in and new-gym limits hit everyone at once
what: Both apps reach the gym server through MettleUp's own address, so a supabase.co block in India cannot stop them. The gym server's limits on wrong PINs (5 per number in 15 minutes) and on new gyms (5 per network address in an hour) count by the sender's network address. Through our address, Cloudflare hands the gym server one shared address for every person (Cloudflare documents this for a Worker calling another Cloudflare site). So anyone who knows an owner's or desk person's mobile can type 5 wrong PINs and lock that person out for 15 minutes, again and again; and after 5 new gyms are made in any one hour, every further new-gym sign-up that hour is refused as busy. A guesser who calls supabase.co directly is not slowed by honest users, but honest users are slowed by him.
expected: Each person's limits count only their own attempts: the person's real address reaches the gym server, and a lock-out by strangers does not stop the real owner.
who: gym owners and desk staff signing in; new gyms signing up
how_often: lock-out only under deliberate abuse; new-gym refusals whenever more than 5 gyms sign up in one hour
fix_line: Send the real caller address from our server in a header only our server can set, and have the database limits read it

title: The 5-wrong-tries limit on WhatsApp sign-in codes can be beaten by sending many guesses at the same moment
what: When a 6-digit Forgot PIN or new-gym code is checked, the server reads how many wrong tries the code has, then writes that number plus one. Guesses sent at the same moment all read the same old number, so far more than 5 guesses can be tried against one code before it dies. A guessed code gives a proof that resets the PIN of that mobile's desk account. Not live today: this way of sending codes is hidden, and 'Verify with WhatsApp' (the person sends us a message) is used instead.
expected: A code dies after 5 wrong guesses however fast they arrive.
who: gym owners and desk staff (Forgot PIN)
how_often: only under deliberate abuse, and only if code sending is switched back on
fix_line: Count a wrong try in one database step that also refuses once the count reaches 5

title: No test proves a member cannot check or pay another member's payment, or that a desk sees only its own gym's payment settings
what: The payment code takes the gym and member only from the signed-in key, and a test proves another gym's desk cannot claim or list a gym's payments. But no test sends another member's key (same gym or another gym) to the member payment check or pay calls, and none checks the payment settings, payment switches or AI allowance tables from another gym's key. Today the code checks correctly; a later change could drop a check with no test failing.
expected: Each payment and allowance table has a test that sends another gym's (and another member's) key and expects a refusal or nothing.
who: members paying in the app
how_often: only if a later change breaks the check
fix_line: Add refusal tests with another member key and another gym key for the member payment calls and the settings tables

title: The watch app ships an old helper library with a known high-rated security flaw
what: The watch app is built with a version of a common Google helper library that has a published high-rated flaw (a crafted saved object can make the app run out of memory). The watch never reads saved objects from outside, so no way to reach the flaw was found; it is still a known-flawed part inside a shipped app, and automatic dependency alerts are switched off for the repository, so nobody is told.
expected: The watch app uses the fixed version of the library (33.7.2 or later), and known flaws in its parts are flagged automatically.
who: members with the watch app
how_often: always present, no known trigger
fix_line: Move the watch's helper library to the fixed version and switch on dependency alerts

title: A stranger can spend a gym's AI credits and fill its chat slots from the gym's web page
what: The AI helper on a gym's web page limits each visitor to 3 AI answers a day, but the visitor is only a random id the browser makes up, and a script can make a new one for every question. From one network address the server then allows 30 questions a day, which is the whole gym's daily allowance of 30 AI answers (3 AI credits) and 30 of the gym's 40 new chats a day. Every one becomes an enquiry in the gym's Enquiries. After that, real visitors get no AI answer that day, and once 40 chats are used they cannot start a chat at all. Over a week this can use up a trial gym's 20 starter credits. Not live today: the chat is behind two switches that are off.
expected: One person cannot use up a gym's daily AI answers, chat slots or credits; the per-visitor limit counts something the visitor cannot reset at will.
who: owners
how_often: when someone tries it
fix_line: Count AI answers per network address as well as per browser id, and keep a few daily answers back for visitors not yet seen

title: A gym's public web page shows its join code, so anyone can join that gym's member app
what: When a gym takes online sign-ups, its public web page carries the gym's join code inside the 'Become a member' link, and search engines can list the page. The same code is what the member app asks for to join the gym; an earlier finding (FN-L3-server-database-1-01) notes that with the code anyone can join as an app member under any name and read the gym's messages, offers and shop. So the code no longer needs guessing: it is printed on the page. The join form itself is safe (it checks the number on WhatsApp and the desk approves), but the member app join is not. Not live today: gym pages are behind a switch that is off.
expected: The public page link opens the join form without handing out the code that lets anyone into the member app, or joining the member app needs the desk's yes.
who: owners and members
how_often: every gym with a web page and online sign-up on
fix_line: Give the page link its own code for the join form only, or make a member app join wait for the desk's approval

title: One person can use up a gym's 'Report this page' allowance for the day
what: 'Report this page' is stopped after 50 reports a day for one gym, counted over everyone. The web server adds 5 a day per network address, but the report can be sent straight to the gym server with the public app key, which skips that. One script can send 50 made-up reports, which fills MettleUp HQ's report list and stops any real report about that gym (a scam, a closed gym) being taken for the rest of the day. Not live today: gym pages are behind a switch that is off.
expected: A real report can always get through; one sender cannot use up the gym's report allowance.
who: MettleUp HQ
how_often: when someone tries it
fix_line: Let only the web server send reports (signed, as the chat does), so its per-address limit always applies

title: The reply helper in HQ sends a person's help question to Google, but the privacy notice says only Anthropic reads help messages
what: When the owner taps the English helper on a reply, the person's whole help question, the earlier AI answer and earlier team replies go to Google Gemini with the draft. The privacy notice says help questions are read by Anthropic's Claude, and its list for Google names only sign-in, pop-ups, Play and the member-list import. The helper refuses a free Google key, so Google does not train on the text, but the sending itself is not told to anyone. It only happens when the helper's key is saved; whether it is saved on the live server could not be checked.
expected: Every outside company that gets a help message is named in the privacy notice, in English and Hindi, before the message is sent there.
who: members and gym staff who send a help question
how_often: each time the owner uses the English helper on a reply
fix_line: Add Google Gemini to the privacy notice for help questions (both languages), or switch the helper to the AI company the notice already names.

title: HQ cannot erase one member: the step says to do it through support access, which can only read
what: A delete request for one member tells the owner to open support access, find the member and erase their details by hand. Support access is read-only, and HQ has no erase button for a member. The only thing HQ does is tick the request as done, and the tick does not check that anything was erased. So a member's erase request can be closed as done with the member's details still in the gym's records.
expected: A member erase request can be finished from HQ (or handed to the gym with a clear step), and it is only marked done once the member's details are really gone.
who: members who ask MettleUp to erase their details
how_often: every member erase request
fix_line: Give HQ a real erase-member action (or a step that asks the gym owner to erase and confirms it), and let the done tick check the member is gone.

title: Deleting a gym for ever leaves its gym web page photos behind, while HQ says nothing is left
what: When a gym is deleted, HQ removes only the gym's logo and shop product pictures. The photos uploaded for the gym's public web page sit in a third, private picture store that the delete never touches. After the delete HQ says the tables were checked and nothing is left, and counts only the pictures it removed. Those photos can show the gym, its trainers and members.
expected: Deleting a gym removes every picture the gym uploaded, and the done message only says nothing is left when that is true.
who: gyms that leave MettleUp and the people in their page photos
how_often: every gym delete where the gym had page photos
fix_line: Remove the gym's web page photo folder as part of the gym delete, and report any photo that could not be removed.

title: A demo request marked won is kept for ever, even after that gym is deleted
what: The nightly clean-up deletes demo requests older than 12 months unless their status is won. A won request has no end date at all: the owner's mobile number, gym name and city stay for good, also after the gym has left MettleUp and been deleted. The status is set by hand in HQ, so one wrong pick of won keeps a stranger's number for ever too.
expected: A won demo request is deleted when its gym is deleted, or after a stated time; the privacy notice says how long.
who: gym owners who asked for a demo and became customers
how_often: every won demo request
fix_line: Give won demo requests an end (for example when the gym is deleted, or a fixed time after winning) and state it in the notice.

title: Deleting a gym does not touch what the second database holds about it
what: The gym delete clears the main database and proves it table by table. The second database (Cloudflare's) is never asked: feedback and help messages sent with that gym's code stay until they are a year old, the gym's AI use rows stay up to a year, and its AI limit rows stay with no end. HQ's done message says nothing is left.
expected: A gym delete also clears, or clearly lists, what the second database still holds for that gym, so the done message is true and the 30-day delete promise covers both places.
who: gyms that leave MettleUp and their staff who sent feedback
how_often: every gym delete
fix_line: On a gym delete, also remove the gym's limit rows and decide (and say on screen) what happens to its feedback and AI use rows.

title: A delete request close to its 30-day limit is not in Needs you
what: The privacy notice promises a delete within 30 days. An open delete request turns red on its own page when 5 days or fewer are left, but it is never counted in Needs you, the menu number, the sound or the pop-up. Once a request is written down nothing reminds the owner, so it can run past day 30 unless he opens the Delete requests page.
expected: An open delete request shows in Needs you, and louder as day 30 gets close.
who: gyms and members who asked for a delete
how_often: every open delete request
fix_line: Count open delete requests in Needs you and mark the ones with few days left.

title: The AI Assistant's history keeps a member's name and typed mobile number for 400 days, out of reach of any member erase
what: Every AI Assistant request is saved with the owner's own words, as typed (mobile numbers and emails are hidden only from the AI, not from this saved copy), and with the drafted change, which can hold a new member's name, mobile number and amount. This copy stays 400 days and is shown again in the assistant's history and credits list. If a member asks the gym to erase them, nothing reaches this copy: it is deleted only when its 400 days are up or the whole gym is deleted. In the test gym 2 of 11 saved requests hold member details.
expected: When a member is erased, their name and number are also cleared from the AI Assistant's saved requests, or the saved copy keeps the hidden form of numbers.
who: members whose details the owner types into the AI Assistant
how_often: every member erase request, once erasing a member exists
fix_line: Include the AI Assistant's saved requests in the member erase, or save them with numbers already hidden

title: The record of who asked the AI is deleted after 400 days only by chance
what: Each AI question is recorded with who asked (a staff or member id, or a coded visitor address) to count credits. Records older than 400 days are deleted only when a new question happens to trigger it (about 1 in 100 questions). The nightly clean-up deletes old AI requests but skips these records. If questions slow or stop, old records stay past 400 days. The privacy notice names the 400 days for requests but says nothing about this record of who asked.
expected: These records are deleted every night once they are 400 days old, like the AI requests, and the notice names them.
who: members, staff and gym page visitors who ask the AI
how_often: whenever questions are few
fix_line: Add these records to the nightly 400-day clean-up and mention them in the privacy notice

title: A gym cannot erase a member's details, though the data agreement says the gym handles erase requests
what: The admin app has no way to delete or blank out a member. Its list of record actions has undo for an import, a check-in and an expense, but nothing for a member. The gym server also refuses to delete any member, plan or receipt typed in by hand; only imported ones can be taken back. The data agreement tells the gym that when a member asks to erase their details, the gym handles it. So a gym that gets such a request has no tool to do it, and HQ has none either (already written for HQ).
expected: An owner can erase one member's personal details (name, mobile, photo and notes), keeping only what tax law needs from receipts, and the member is gone from every desk.
who: members who ask their gym to erase their details, and gym owners
how_often: every member erase request
fix_line: Add an owner-only erase-member action that blanks the person's details on the server and on every desk, and keeps receipts without the name.

title: A deleted record keeps all its details on the server for ever
what: When the panel deletes a record (an undone import of members and receipts, a check-in, an expense), the server only marks it deleted and keeps the whole record, with the member's name and mobile, hidden but in the database. The first version of this step blanked the record; a later version dropped that, and nothing cleans these rows later. So an owner who undoes a wrong import believes those people are gone, but their details stay on MettleUp's server and in its backups.
expected: A deleted record keeps only an empty marker (as the first version did), so nothing personal stays once the gym deletes it.
who: members whose records a gym deletes, mainly after an undone import
how_often: every delete from the panel
fix_line: Blank the record's details when it is marked deleted, and blank the ones already marked.

title: After a gym goes online, its old browser copy of every member stays on that computer for ever, even after sign out
what: When a gym kept in one browser is put online, the browser's own copy of the gym (all members, mobiles, plans, payments and check-ins) is moved aside under a dated name and is never deleted. Signing out clears the online copy but not this one. The privacy notice says signing a device out deletes the copy the admin app keeps on it. On a shared front-desk computer this full member list stays behind, unseen, after the gym has left or the staff member has gone.
expected: Once the records are safely online, the old browser copy is deleted (or at the latest on sign out), as the notice says.
who: members of gyms that started in one browser and then went online
how_often: every gym that went online from a browser-only gym
fix_line: Delete the set-aside browser copy once the upload is confirmed, or on sign out, and say so on screen.

title: Unsent desk work stays on a computer with no end date after the person is removed or signed out
what: New members, member changes, payments and check-ins made without internet wait on the device until they are sent. When the person is removed or signed out from another device, the device forgets its key and copy but keeps these waiting items, with members' names and mobiles, until someone from the same gym signs in there again, which may be never. The sign-out box says refused items stay, but the privacy notice says signing out deletes the device's copy, and a removed person's device is told nothing.
expected: The notice says unsent items stay on the device until sent, and they have an end (for example removed after a set time with a warning to the owner).
who: members whose details were typed at a desk while offline
how_often: rare: only when unsent items remain at removal or sign out
fix_line: Name unsent items in the privacy notice and give them an end date with a warning to the owner.

title: A removed staff member's name, mobile and every device they signed in on are kept for ever
what: Removing a person from the panel only stamps them as removed: their name and mobile stay in the staff list, and every sign-in they made (which device, when first and last seen) stays too. No clean-up ever deletes these. The privacy notice says sign-in records are kept 7 days, and has no line for how long a removed staff member's details are kept.
expected: A removed person's details and old sign-ins are deleted after a stated time (sign-ins after 7 days, as the notice says), and the notice says how long a removed staff member is kept.
who: former gym staff
how_often: every person removed from a gym
fix_line: Add a nightly clean-up for ended sign-ins and for removed staff after a stated time, and add that time to the notice.

title: Photos an owner takes off the gym web page are kept on our server for ever
what: When an owner removes a photo from the gym web page, only the link to it is dropped. The picture file stays in the private photo store with no end date. Nobody can open it any more, but no clean-up job exists to delete it, and the notice gives no keeping time for these photos. Photos can show the gym, its trainers and members. Live today the store holds no photos at all, so nothing is kept yet.
expected: A photo the owner removes is deleted from our server soon after (or the notice says how long removed photos are kept).
