who: gym owners, and trainers or members shown in page photos
how_often: every photo removed from a gym web page
fix_line: Add the planned clean-up that deletes photo files no web page uses any more, for example each night.

title: Anyone with the app key can list the photos of every gym web page, even pages the owner never published
what: The read rule for gym web page photos also answers the storage list call. The key that unlocks it ships inside every MettleUp app and web page, so anyone can list and open the photos on every gym page row, including drafts the owner has not published. The rule was written knowing this. Live today no gym has page photos, so nothing is exposed yet.
expected: A photo can be opened only by its own gym, or by the public once that gym page is published; it cannot be listed across gyms.
who: gym owners writing a web page draft, and people in those photos
how_often: whenever someone uses the public key to list the photo store
fix_line: Let the public read only photos of published pages, and keep draft photos to the gym itself (or block listing).

title: An old switched-off path still lets a member phone send body weight, calories and protein to the gym, against the privacy notice
what: An early version sent the gym a summary per member with body weight, today's calories and protein and last meal time. The phone feature is switched off, the old owner screen that read it is no longer opened, and the table is empty live. But the table and its rules are still on the server: a member account can still write such a row and the owner and trainers can read it. The privacy notice says body weight and food never go to the gym. The row is only deleted when the whole account is deleted, not when the member leaves the gym.
expected: No server table can carry members' body weight or food for the gym unless the notice says so; unused tables and screens are removed.
who: members
how_often: not today (feature off, table empty); only if an old phone build or a hand-made call writes a row
fix_line: Remove the old summary table with its rules, the old owner screen and the switched-off phone code.

title: The desk can add a child as a member, with photo, birthday and address, while the privacy notice says MettleUp holds no data of anyone under 18
what: Add member accepts any date of birth that is a real day and not in the future, so a 12 or 15 year old can be added with a desk photo, mobile, address and emergency contact. Nothing warns the desk, asks for a parent's yes, or marks the member as a child. These records sit on MettleUp's server. The privacy notice says MettleUp is only for people aged 18 or over and that data of anyone under 18 is deleted once known, yet here the birthday itself tells MettleUp the person is under 18 and nothing deletes it. India's data law asks for a parent's checkable yes before a child's data is handled.
expected: Either the desk is told, when a birthday shows someone under 18, to get a parent's yes (and the gym's records of children are allowed and named in the notice), or the notice's under-18 line says it covers only the member app and not the gym's own records.
who: gyms with members under 18, and those members' parents
how_often: every time the desk adds someone under 18
fix_line: Decide how gyms handle members under 18: add a parent's-yes step on Add member when the birthday shows under 18, and make the notice's under-18 line match.

title: The member-list import shows Google's AI real names from some columns, while the privacy notice says names are hidden
what: Before up to 5 example rows of a gym's old member file go to Google Gemini (or Claude), name and address columns are swapped for a placeholder. But a column whose heading holds a word such as trainer, coach, no, number, ID, code or from is always sent as it is, even when its cells are people's names. So a 'Trainer' column, a 'Father / Guardian name and contact no' column, an 'Emergency contact name (mobile no)' column or a 'Referred by member ID' column sends real names (mobiles stay masked). A free-text remarks column that does not look like a name or an address, such as 'BP patient since 2020', is also sent word for word, so health notes can go out. The server repeats the same rule, so it catches none of this. The privacy notice says names, addresses, mobiles, emails and ID numbers are hidden and only plan names, amounts and dates are not.
expected: No person's name and no health note from the file ever reaches the AI, whatever the column heading says; or the privacy notice says plainly which kinds of columns are sent as they are.
who: gym members, their family contacts and trainers named in an imported file
how_often: each AI import of a file with such a column
fix_line: Hide the cells of every column that is not a plan, amount, date or batch column, whatever its heading, or change the notice to say what is sent.

title: A diet plan sent to named members can never be deleted, though the gym terms say plans can be deleted at any time
what: A diet plan can be addressed to members by name and carries free-text notes from the trainer. The gym can only withdraw it: it stays on MettleUp's server for ever with the list of members it was sent to, also after those members leave the gym. The gym terms tell owners they can change, delete or add plans at any time.
expected: The gym can delete a diet plan for good, and a member's name comes off a plan when the member is removed from the gym.
who: gym owners and the members a plan was sent to
how_often: every diet plan
fix_line: Add a real delete for diet plans and drop removed members from a plan's list.

title: "Never sees money totals" for front desk staff is only true on screen
what: When the owner adds a front desk person, the admin app says they never see money totals. The screens do hide the totals. But every signed-in device, the desk's included, is sent the gym's whole record copy: every receipt, every expense and every plan sold. Anyone at the desk with a little know-how can add them up from the browser. The code itself notes this as a known limit.
expected: Either the desk's copy leaves out what only the owner may see, or the line says the totals are hidden from the desk's screens, not kept from their device.
who: gym owners who rely on staff not knowing the takings
how_often: every gym with a desk login
fix_line: Soften the line now to say the totals are not shown to the desk; later, send the desk a copy without the receipts and expenses it does not need

title: Ready offer messages send a hand-typed saving or family discount that nothing checks or gives
what: The "Longer plan saves money" message goes to members with a plan length, price and saving that the owner types by hand. Nothing compares them with the gym's real plans, so a wrong saving or price goes out to every member as typed. The "Join together and save" message promises a discount for 2 or more family members on any plan until a date, but no sale screen gives that discount or ends it on the date: the desk must remember to cut the price.
expected: The saving is worked out from the gym's own plans (as the one-to-one renewal message already does), and a promised family discount is offered at the sale until the date in the message.
who: members who read a price claim, and the gym that must honour it
how_often: each time an owner sends these ready messages
fix_line: Fill the longer-plan numbers from the gym's plans, and either apply the family discount at the sale or say it is given at the desk

title: The renewal message says "save over paying month by month" when the saving is against the member's own longer plan
what: For a member already on a 3- or 6-month plan, the renewal message works out the saving of a longer plan against renewing that same 3- or 6-month plan, but its words say the saving is against paying month by month. The number shown is then not the saving the words describe (usually smaller).
expected: The words match the sum: "over renewing your current plan" for a member not on a monthly plan, or the saving is worked out against the monthly plan.
who: members on plans longer than a month
how_often: each renewal message to such a member
fix_line: Change the words for members not on a monthly plan to "over renewing your current plan"

title: The fees reminder tells members to pay "on UPI" when the gym has no UPI ID saved
what: The WhatsApp fees reminder always says "Please pay at the front desk or on UPI". When the gym has saved no UPI ID, no UPI ID or pay link follows, so the member is told to pay on UPI with nothing to pay to. A test even pins this sentence for a gym with no UPI ID.
expected: With no UPI ID saved, the reminder says only "Please pay at the front desk".
who: members of gyms with no UPI ID saved
how_often: every fees reminder at such a gym
fix_line: Drop "or on UPI" when the gym has no UPI ID, in English and Hindi

title: The welcome message can name one plan and give the end date of another
what: The welcome message names the plan running today, but the "runs till" date is the end of all the member's plans together, renewals included. When a member has a second plan sold ahead, the message names the first plan with the second plan's end date.
expected: The plan named and the date given belong to the same plan, or the line says "Your membership runs till".
who: members sold two plans at once
how_often: rare
fix_line: Say "Your membership runs till" when more than one plan is ahead

title: The gym agreement says nothing about the public gym web page, which is on for every gym by default
what: The admin app will tell owners they get a free public web page with their fees, timings and photos, and that it is on by default. The gym part of the terms never mentions this page: not that MettleUp shows the gym's words and photos to the public, not that the owner must only upload photos they may use (for example members' faces with their OK), and not that MettleUp can switch a gym's page off. The page switch is already live in the database; only the global switch keeps pages hidden today.
expected: Before pages switch on, the gym terms say that MettleUp publishes the gym's page and photos, that the gym is responsible for having the right to every photo and for members' consent to appear in them, and that MettleUp may switch a page off.
who: gym owners, and members who appear in gym photos
how_often: every gym, once gym web pages switch on
fix_line: Add a short gym web page section to the gym terms (what is published, photo rights and member consent, MettleUp may switch it off) before switching pages on.

title: Entry machine records would be kept for ever, and erasing a member would not reach them
what: The entry machine feature (built, not switched on yet) keeps every finger or face punch, each member's machine number, and the machine's finished job list, which carries the member's name and plan dates. Nothing ever deletes a punch or a finished job, and erasing or archiving a member does not remove their punches or machine number. Only removing the whole machine or deleting the whole gym clears them.
expected: Punches and finished machine jobs have a stated end date and a clean-up, and erasing a member also removes their machine number and punches.
who: members of gyms that will use an entry machine
how_often: every punch, once the feature is switched on
fix_line: Add a nightly clean-up for old punches and finished jobs, and remove a member's machine number and punches when the member is erased, before switching entry machines on.

title: The privacy notice says nothing about entry machine punches
what: Once entry machines are switched on, MettleUp's server will store each member's door punches (time, machine, how they were checked) and send their name and plan dates to the machine. The privacy notice has no line about entry machines: not what is kept, not who sees it, not how long. It only mentions gym machine use for busy machines, which is a different thing.
expected: Before entry machines go live, the privacy notice (English and Hindi) says what punch records MettleUp keeps for the gym, for how long, and how a member gets them erased.
who: members of gyms that will use an entry machine
how_often: from the day entry machines are switched on
fix_line: Add an entry machine line to the privacy notice and its keep-for table, in both languages, before switching the feature on.

title: A person who only asked about joining can never be removed from the gym's enquiry list
what: The Enquiries page lets the owner or desk mark someone "Not interested", but there is no way to delete an enquiry. The server refuses to delete any enquiry, so the name, mobile number, question, follow-up notes and reason stay on MettleUp's server and in its backups for as long as the gym uses MettleUp. These people never became members. If one of them asks the gym to erase their details, the gym cannot do it, though the data agreement says the gym handles erase requests. India's data law also asks that details be erased once their purpose (a possible sale) is over.
expected: The gym can delete an enquiry and the server really removes it; old not-interested enquiries are cleared after a set time that the privacy notice states.
who: people who asked a gym about joining, and gym owners
how_often: every enquiry, for ever
fix_line: Add a delete for an enquiry that really removes it on the server, and a time limit for old not-interested enquiries

title: A gym that turns its shop off, or starts its demo over, leaves its members' names and shop orders on our server for ever
what: A gym kept only in the browser can turn on the shop. That makes a real gym on MettleUp's server with a gym code; members join it with their name and place shop orders there. 'Disconnect the shop' (and, for a demo gym, 'Start over') only makes this browser forget the key. The gym, the members who joined and their orders stay on the server, nothing deletes them later (the nightly clean-up only removes test gyms named 'QA ...'), and the owner has no button left to delete them, because 'Delete the gym' is offered only to gyms that are online. The screen does not say the server copy stays.
expected: Turning the shop off deletes the gym's shop, its joined members and its orders from our server (or the owner is told they stay and how to have them deleted), as the privacy notice promises deletion when a gym leaves.
who: members of a browser-only gym that turned the shop on, and the gym owner
how_often: every time an owner disconnects the shop or starts a demo over
fix_line: When the shop is turned off, delete the gym copy on our server (or tell the owner it stays and give a way to delete it); clean up abandoned demo gyms too.

title: Settings says the gym is 'saved in this browser only' and 'a demo gym is never put online', while its shop part sits on our server
what: A gym that is not online is told 'Your gym is saved in this browser only' and 'Saved in this browser only'; a demo gym is told 'A demo gym is never put online'. But every demo gym, and every browser-only gym that turned on the shop, has a gym on MettleUp's server with its name, gym code, products, the members who joined in the app and their orders. The member list and payments do stay in the browser, so the words are true only for part of the data.
expected: The words say what is on our server: the members list stays in this browser, but the shop, the gym code and members who joined in the app are kept online.
who: owners of a browser-only or demo gym
how_often: every time the Settings page is opened by such a gym
fix_line: Change the 'saved in this browser only' lines to name the shop part that is kept online when the shop is on.

title: When the gym removes a member, the member's desk photo and body measurements stay on the server with no end
what: The gym removes a member by marking them deleted on its list. Nothing then deletes that member's photo taken at the desk or the body measurements the trainer saved. Saving new ones is refused for a removed member, but the old photo and measurements stay until the whole gym is deleted. Body measurements are health data. The privacy notice says the gym's records about a member are kept as long as the gym keeps them, and the gym thinks it no longer keeps this member.
expected: Removing a member also removes their desk photo and body measurements (or after a short, stated time to allow undo), and the notice says how long they stay.
who: members a gym removes from its list
how_often: every removed member who had a desk photo or measurements
fix_line: When a member is removed for good, delete their desk photo and measurements too, and state the time in the notice.

title: Trainer questions, trainer summaries and sent workout reports are only deleted when someone opens them again
what: The privacy notice promises questions to a trainer go after 180 days, the trainer summary after 90 days with no update, and a sent workout report after 30 days. No timed job does any of this: the nightly clean-up never touches these three. Each is removed only when the member or someone at that gym next opens that list. If a gym stops using the feature, or the member stops opening the app, the old questions, workout summaries and report files stay on the server. Member messages to the gym have the same gap (already written down separately).
expected: These are deleted on a schedule at the promised time, whoever opens the app.
who: members who asked a trainer, shared a summary or sent a workout report
how_often: whenever the gym or member stops opening that list
fix_line: Add these three deletions to the nightly clean-up.

title: The MettleUp access card can say 'MettleUp has never opened your records' when it did, more than 2 years ago
what: The owner's MettleUp access card shows 'MettleUp has never opened your records' whenever its list is empty. The list only holds support windows and MettleUp actions from the last 2 years, and the nightly clean-up deletes older ones. So a gym whose records were opened more than 2 years ago is told they were never opened. The sentence also ignores direct database looks, which the card never reads (already written as a separate finding).
expected: The empty line says what is true, for example 'MettleUp has not opened your records in the last 2 years', matching the 2-year keep time in the privacy notice.
who: gym owners
how_often: only for gyms whose last support look is over 2 years old
fix_line: Change the empty-list sentence to say 'in the last 2 years' (and count direct looks once the card shows them).

title: Delete my account says everything on MettleUp's server is deleted, but a gym member's workouts shared with the gym stay
what: Before and after the delete, the app tells the member that their account and everything saved on MettleUp's server is deleted. The delete only removes the saved copy, the member's account and its profile. For a member who is in a gym, the trainer summary of their workouts, their leaderboard totals, machine use, shared workouts and questions to a trainer all stay on MettleUp's server, because they hang off the gym link, not the account. When the account is kept because the gym also uses that sign-in, the older activity summary and the profile stay too, while the screen still says everything saved on MettleUp is deleted. The privacy notice gets this right (leave the gym to delete those), but the app's own words do not.
expected: The delete words say exactly what goes and what stays (for a gym member: leave the gym to delete what the gym has), or the delete also clears what the member shared with the gym.
who: members in a gym who delete their MettleUp account
how_often: every account delete by a gym member
fix_line: Change the delete words to say the gym's copies stay until you leave the gym, or clear them as part of the delete.

title: A member who types an age of 10 to 17 can sign in and have their age and body weight kept on MettleUp's server
what: The profile accepts any age from 10. Signing in with Google is offered to every member with no age line, and the saved copy then sends the profile, including the age, and the body weight to MettleUp's server. Nothing checks the age, so the server knowingly holds health-type data of someone who said they are under 18. The privacy notice and terms say MettleUp is only for people 18 or over and that such data is deleted once MettleUp learns of it.
expected: Ages under 18 are refused (or sign-in is blocked for them), or the saved copy is not kept for a profile under 18, matching the notice.
who: members under 18 who sign in with Google
how_often: every under-18 member who signs in
fix_line: Make 18 the lowest age the app accepts, or stop the saved copy for a profile under 18.

title: If the hidden AI coach is switched back on, members' spoken messages go to the phone's speech service and their chat goes to an AI, and the privacy notice names neither
what: The coach chat is off today, so nothing is sent. But its mic button uses the phone's built-in speech recogniser without asking it to stay on the phone; on most Android phones that sends the voice to Google. The typed or spoken message then goes to the coach AI. The privacy notice only lists Groq for spoken feedback and spoken AI Assistant requests, and its Google line does not mention speech or a member-facing coach. Flipping the one coach switch would start these sends with no notice change.
expected: Before the coach is switched on, the privacy notice (English and Hindi) names where a member's spoken and typed coach messages go, or the speech stays on the phone.
who: members, only once the coach is switched on
how_often: never today; every coach message after the switch is turned on
fix_line: Add a privacy-notice check to the coach switch-on list, or ask the speech recogniser to work on the phone only.

title: A member who turned on photo backup can no longer find the switch to turn it off
what: The 'Include photos in my backup' switch now sits on a page that no Settings row opens. A member who turned it on earlier keeps it on: at every app start and after every new photo, the newest progress photos are copied into Android's backup to their Google account, and the Progress photos page even says their newest photos are in the phone's backup. There is no way in the app to stop it except erasing everything.
expected: Anyone who has the photo backup on can find the switch and turn it off as easily as they turned it on (or the app turns it off and deletes the copies now that the switch was taken away).
who: members who turned on photo backup before it was hidden
how_often: every new progress photo, for as long as they use the app
fix_line: Put the photo backup switch back where members can reach it, or turn it off for everyone and delete the copies.

title: The privacy notice says everything you log stays on your phone, but Android's backup copies it to the member's Google account
what: The app's backup rules let Android copy the whole workout record (workouts, routines, body weight, measurements, profile) and the app's settings to the member's Google account whenever backup is on in the phone's settings, which is the usual default. The only place in the app that said so is now on a hidden page. The privacy notice says everything you log stays on your phone unless you sign in or join a gym.
expected: The privacy notice (both languages) says Android's own backup may copy the app's records to the member's own Google account, and how to switch it off.
who: every member on Android with phone backup on
how_often: every day the phone backs up
fix_line: Add one line on Android's own backup to the privacy notice in English and Hindi.

title: Erase all data says it worked even when progress photos or the profile photo could not be deleted
what: Erase all data deletes the photo records first, then tries to delete the progress photo, backup copy and profile photo files. If that file delete fails, the failure is swallowed and nothing is reported, unlike workout photos and exercise videos, which are named when they stay. The member is told the phone is back to new while body photos can still sit in the app's storage.
expected: A failed delete of progress photos or the profile photo is named in the 'left behind' line, like the other files, so the member can try again.
who: members who erase the phone
how_often: rarely (only when a file delete fails)
fix_line: Make the photo file delete a reported erase step, so a failure is named and can be retried.

title: Loading the demo says the member's photos are deleted, but their own exercise photos and videos stay on the phone
what: The hidden demo switch warns that the member's workouts, profile, routines, body weight, measurements and photos are deleted. The load wipes the records and the progress and workout photo files, but not the photos and videos the member added to their own exercises. Those files stay in the app's storage with nothing pointing at them. The progress photo file delete is also silent if it fails.
expected: Loading the demo deletes every photo and video file of the member's, as the warning says.
who: staff or members who use the hidden demo switch
how_often: each demo load on a phone with exercise photos
fix_line: Delete the exercise photos and videos folder when the demo loads too.

title: Turning photo backup off deletes the copies on the phone, but the copy already in Google's backup stays until Android backs up again
what: The card says turning it off deletes the copies. The app deletes its own backup folder at once, but the photos already sent to the member's Google account stay there until Android's next backup run, which Android times itself (often a day or more).
expected: The card says the copies in the phone's Google backup go at Android's next backup, or the app asks Android to back up again soon.
who: members who turn photo backup off
how_often: each time it is turned off
fix_line: Say that the Google backup copy goes at Android's next backup.

title: The 'Your workouts are only on this phone' card is not true for gym members or phones with Android backup on
what: After the third workout, a member with no MettleUp account sees a card saying their workouts are only on this phone. But a member who joined a gym has workout sharing with trainers switched on at joining, so the phone sends the gym each workout's day, name, heaviest set per exercise and set count for up to a year. And Android's own backup copies the whole workout record to the member's Google account whenever backup is on in the phone's settings. The card is meant as a warning about losing data, but it tells the member something about where their data is that is wrong.
expected: The card only says the workouts are only on this phone when that is true, or it says plainly what else holds a copy (the gym, if sharing is on; the phone's Google backup, if on).
who: members without a MettleUp account, mostly gym members
how_often: every member who reaches 3 workouts without signing in
fix_line: Reword the card to say that losing this phone loses the workouts, without claiming nowhere else holds them, or give gym members who share a different line.

title: The Health Connect page says only workouts logged in MettleUp are sent, but imported workouts are sent too
what: Under Send past workouts the app says only workouts logged in MettleUp are sent. But workouts brought in from a Hevy or Strong file are sent to Health Connect by themselves right after the import, whenever sending is on. And when the phone cannot tell when MettleUp first ran, every workout on the phone is sent, old ones included, with no such line. The data only goes to Health Connect on the member's own phone, so nothing reaches another company, but the line tells the member something that is not true.
expected: The words under Send past workouts match what is really sent: they also name imported workouts, or imported workouts follow the same rule.
who: members who send workouts to Health Connect and import a Hevy or Strong file
how_often: every import while Health Connect sending is on
fix_line: Change the line to say imported workouts are sent too, or hold imported workouts back the same way.

title: Weigh-ins from Health Connect would reach the gym and an AI if two switched-off features came back
what: Weigh-ins read from Health Connect go into the same body-weight log as typed ones, with no lasting mark of where they came from. Two features that are switched off today read the newest body weight from that log: the old gym sync puts it in a summary the gym's dashboard shows in its member list, and the AI coach gets it in its day snapshot. The privacy notice promises Health Connect data never goes to the gym or to any AI, and the gym table in the notice does not list body weight at all. Nothing is sent today because both switches are off.
expected: Before either feature is turned on again, weigh-ins that came from Health Connect are left out of what goes to the gym and to the AI, or the notice and Health Connect's rules allow it.
who: members who let MettleUp read weight from Health Connect
how_often: only if gym sync or the AI coach is switched back on
fix_line: Keep a mark on weigh-ins from Health Connect and leave them out of anything sent to the gym or an AI; add a test that blocks it.

title: Phone sign-in says the number is not kept, but after joining the gym it is saved on the member's gym link
what: The phone sign-in screen says 'Your number is checked once and is not kept for this', and the privacy notice says the same. When the member then joins the gym the search found (by tapping Join, or going straight in), the app hands the proof in and the server writes the proven number, twice, onto the member's link to that gym, with the time it was checked. It stays there until the member leaves, and another finding shows leaving does not clear the check-in copy. The gym already has the same number on its member list, so no new party sees it, which is why this is not marked S1; but the words promise something the system does not do.
expected: Either the number is not written anywhere by the sign-in, or the screen and the notice say plainly that the checked number is saved on your link to the gym until you leave it.
who: members who sign in with their phone number and join the found gym
how_often: every phone sign-in that ends in a join
fix_line: Change the screen and notice words to say the checked number is saved on your gym link until you leave, or stop writing it there.

title: Phone sign-in says 'we never message you', but MettleUp replies on WhatsApp after the check
what: The WhatsApp step tells the member 'You pay nothing, and we never message you.' When the member's message arrives, the server sends a WhatsApp reply back to that number: a 'your number is verified' message, or a 'we could not find your code' message. It is a reply to their own message, not marketing, and it only goes out when the WhatsApp sending key is set and Meta allows it. The privacy notice does not mention the reply either.
expected: The screen does not promise 'we never message you' while the check sends a reply; it says, for example, that MettleUp replies once to confirm and sends nothing else.
who: members who sign in with their phone number
how_often: every phone check, while the reply key is set
fix_line: Reword the line to say MettleUp replies once to confirm the check and never messages you otherwise.

title: Bringing back a Google Drive backup on the welcome screen warns only about workouts, but also deletes routines and body records
what: After 'Remove demo data' a member's own routines, body weight, measurements and photos can stay on the phone. When the member brings back a Drive backup from the welcome screen, the warning says only how many workouts are deleted, and if there are no workouts it asks nothing at all. The restore replaces everything: routines, body weight, measurements, exercise choices and the profile photo go too. A safety copy is taken first, so the data can be got back, but the member is not told what goes. This is the same kind of gap as the demo-load sheet in an earlier finding, on a different button.
expected: The restore warning names everything that is replaced (workouts, routines, body records, photos) and is shown whenever anything of the member's is on the phone.
who: members who removed the demo and then bring back a Drive backup
how_often: rare: only after a demo was removed
fix_line: Count everything that will be replaced and show the warning whenever the count is above zero.

title: Erase all data keeps the free month's start day and the first-run date, though the notice says everything on the phone is removed
what: The privacy notice says Erase all data removes everything the app holds on the phone. On purpose, the erase keeps the day this phone's free month started and the date the app first ran here. Neither holds a name, number or workout, but the next person to use the phone inherits a used-up free month, and the notice's 'everything' is not quite true.
expected: The notice says the erase keeps the free-month start day (so the free month is not given twice), or the erase clears it.
who: members who erase the phone, and the next person to use it
how_often: every erase
fix_line: Add one line to the notice and the erase screen saying the free-month start day stays on the phone.

title: Find my gym also sends the member's first name, and its 'not kept' line clashes with the privacy notice
what: To look for the member's gym, the app sends the proven mobile number and the member's first name to MettleUp's server, which matches both against gym member lists. The privacy notice says only that the number is looked for. The screen also says the number is checked once and is not kept, while the notice says WhatsApp number checks are kept for 2 days in a coded form. A member reading both gets two different stories.
expected: The privacy notice names every detail Find my gym sends (number and first name), and the screen line and the notice say the same thing about how long the number check is kept.
who: members who use Find my gym
how_often: every Find my gym search, once the feature is switched on
fix_line: Add the first name to the Find my gym lines of the notice (both languages) and make the screen line match the 2-day coded check.

title: What my gym can see says the app never sends which exercises you did, even while gym-mate sharing sends them
what: The page's opening text says MettleUp never sends which exercises you did. The page only drops that line when the gym has busy machines on or when the trainer view has loaded. The gym-mate sharing switch sits on the same page, and when it is on the app sends up to 30 workouts with the best set of each exercise. So a member who turned on gym-mate sharing reads, on the very page where they switched it on, that their exercises are never sent. The same happens if the trainer view could not be read (for example with no signal) while trainer sharing is on.
expected: The opening text only says what is true for this member right now: when gym-mate or trainer sharing is on, it says which exercises and sets are sent and to whom.
who: gym members who share workouts with gym mates or trainers
how_often: every visit to the page while such sharing is on and busy machines is off
fix_line: Pick the opening text from every sharing switch that is on, not just busy machines and the trainer view.

title: The 'What my gym can see' page says MettleUp never sends which exercises you did, even while the member shares workouts with gym mates
what: In a gym without busy machines or the trainer view, the page opens with: MettleUp never sends which exercises you did, your body weight, photos or notes. Right under it sits the switch to let gym mates see your workouts. When that switch is on, the app sends up to 30 workouts with each exercise's name and best set, and other members can open them. The page keeps the never-sends-exercises line while this is happening. The switch's own caption tells the truth, so the page says two different things.
expected: While gym-mate sharing is on (or can be switched on), the page uses the line without the exercises claim, as it already does for busy machines and the trainer view.
who: members of a gym with gym-mate profiles on
how_often: every visit to that page
fix_line: Show the shorter line (no exercises claim) whenever gym-mate sharing is on or offered

title: Find my gym says we never message you, but MettleUp's WhatsApp number writes back after the check
what: The Find my gym screen tells the member: You pay nothing, and we never message you. When the member's WhatsApp message arrives, MettleUp's WhatsApp number sends a reply saying the number is verified, and a different reply when the code is missing. So the member does get a message from MettleUp, right after being told they never would.
expected: The screen's words match what happens, for example: We reply once to say it worked, and never message you after that.
who: members who use Find my gym
how_often: every check
fix_line: Change the line to say MettleUp replies once to confirm, and never messages after that

title: The privacy notice says the trainer summary holds 3 months of workouts, but the app now sends up to a year
what: When sharing with trainers is on, the app sends the gym every workout since the member joined, up to the last 12 months and up to 400 workouts, each with its name, every exercise's heaviest set and how many sets. The app's own caption says 12 months. The privacy notice, in English and Hindi, still says the summary holds up to 30 workouts from the last 3 months.
expected: The privacy notice says the same as the app: up to 12 months of workouts since joining the gym.
who: members of a gym whose server takes the 12-month progress
how_often: every trainer share
fix_line: Update the trainer summary line of the privacy notice in both languages to 12 months since joining

title: The workout offer's consent screen says the gym never gets your exercises, weights or sets, but other sharing already sends them
what: The offer's consent screen says the gym gets only the dates of workouts and never the exercises, weights or sets. The offer itself keeps to that. But on joining a gym the app switches on sharing with trainers, which sends each exercise's heaviest set and the number of sets, and busy machines (on unless the member turns it off) sends which exercises were done with the day and hour. A member who reads the offer screen is told something about the gym that is not true for their account.
expected: The offer screen says only what the offer sends, for example that the offer itself sends only dates, without saying the gym never gets exercises, weights or sets.
who: members who see a workout offer
how_often: every offer consent screen
fix_line: Reword the offer's line to say the offer sends only dates, and point to the other sharing switches

title: Sharing that starts on its own at joining rests on legitimate interest, a reason India's data law does not have
what: Joining a gym switches on three kinds of sharing without a yes: workouts for trainers, which machines are used, and the pop-up code. The privacy notice gives legitimate interest as the reason and says the member can object. India's data protection law allows personal data use with consent or for a short list of legitimate uses; it has no general legitimate interest. The workout sharing goes to the gym, which can see a member's training history for a year.
expected: Each sharing either asks for a clear yes at joining, or the notice names a reason the Indian law accepts, checked by a lawyer.
who: every member who joins a gym
how_often: every join
fix_line: Ask a lawyer; likely turn the trainer and machine sharing into a tick box at joining

title: The gym news notification group also carries trainer replies, but its description says only news
what: Android shows the group's description as news from the gym: a holiday, new timings or an offer. Trainer replies to a member's workout question pop up in the same group. A member who turns the group off in the phone's settings to stop news also stops trainer replies, without being told.
expected: The description names everything the group carries, or trainer replies get their own group.
who: members who ask a trainer a question
how_often: when they change the phone's notification settings
fix_line: Add trainer replies to the group's description

title: The gym messages switch says a pop-up can take a few minutes, but without instant push it takes 15 minutes or more
what: The switch's line says a gym message can take a few minutes to arrive. When the instant push is not working on that phone or server, the app's background check runs at most every 15 minutes, and Android can push it later still.
expected: The line gives a time that holds when the instant push is missing, such as up to 15 minutes or more.
who: members whose phone has no instant push
how_often: each gym message
fix_line: Say it can take up to 15 minutes or more

title: 'Deleted for good' is not quite true for a removed workout photo
what: Removing a workout photo asks 'It is deleted from this workout and from the app for good.' Two gaps. A backup file the member saved earlier still holds the photo, and restoring that backup puts it back on the workout. And the app deletes the photo's record first and the picture file second; if the file delete fails, the failure is only logged, the member is told nothing, and the start-up clean-up never finds the file again because it looks for records, not files. The picture then stays in the app's folder until 'Erase all data'.
expected: The words match what happens: say that copies in backups you saved before are not touched, and make sure a picture file whose delete failed is cleaned up later (or the member is told).
who: members who remove a workout photo
how_often: rare: only after restoring an older backup, or when a file delete fails
fix_line: Add 'copies in backups you saved before stay there' to the remove pop-up, and have the start-up clean-up also delete workout photo files that no record points at.

title: Erase all data leaves four workout settings behind on the phone
what: Erase all data is meant to leave the phone like a fresh install, and the privacy notice says it removes everything the app holds on the phone. It resets the main workout settings, but four smaller saved choices stay: the gym's plates and bar setup, the muscle tip choices (snoozed or skipped muscles), the rest alert choices and which routine folders are open. None of them holds a name, a workout or a photo, so the next person to use the phone only inherits these choices.
expected: Erase all data resets every saved choice of the workout part of the app, so nothing of the last person is left.
who: members who erase the app to hand the phone on
how_often: every Erase all data
fix_line: Add the four saved choices to the settings reset that Erase all data already runs.

title: Exercise demo films are fetched from GitHub, which the privacy notice does not list for that
what: The first time a member opens an exercise that has a demo film, the phone downloads it straight from a public GitHub page. GitHub then sees the phone's internet address and which exercise was opened, each time a new film is fetched. The privacy notice lists GitHub only as the place for crash reports with personal details removed, and says it names every company that helps MettleUp. Nothing about the member's name, gym or workouts is sent.
expected: Every outside company that a phone talks to is named in the privacy notice (both languages) for what it really does, or the films come from a server the notice already names.
who: members who open an exercise with a demo film
how_often: once per film per phone
fix_line: Serve the demo films from MettleUp's own web host (already listed), or add the film downloads to GitHub's line in the notice in English and Hindi.

title: Importing routines from a Hevy share link opens Hevy's web page inside the app, and the privacy notice does not name Hevy
what: When a member pastes a Hevy share link, the app quietly opens Hevy's public web page in a hidden in-app browser and reads the routines off it. That page load sends the phone's internet address and device details to Hevy (and to anything Hevy's page itself loads). No Hevy account is used and nothing the member logged is sent, but the privacy notice's list of outside companies does not mention Hevy or that the app opens its page.
expected: The privacy notice says that importing from a Hevy link opens Hevy's own page from the phone, so Hevy sees the phone's address, in English and Hindi.
who: members who import routines from a Hevy link
how_often: each Hevy link import
fix_line: Add one line to the privacy notice (both languages) that a Hevy link import opens Hevy's page from the phone.

title: Every cloud phone test leaves made-up gyms on the live server for ever, with real-looking mobile numbers in them
what: The release-gate phone test, the cross-role journeys and the conditions test each make fresh gyms on the live server, owned by 'QA Owner' with the mobile 98765 00001, and some add members or imports with 98765 00002, 00021, 00022, 00031 and 00032. There is no way for a test to delete what it made, so the gyms and those people rows stay in the live database after every run; they are only hidden from HQ's list by their 'QA' name and listed in the run's evidence for a manual sweep. Those numbers are in a normal Indian mobile range, so they may belong to real people who never agreed to be stored, and a real owner of 98765 00001 would be treated as an existing gym owner (no free trial) if they signed up with a phone check.
expected: Test runs on the live server use numbers that can never be a real person's, and every gym and member a test makes is removed at the end of the run (or by a regular sweep), so test data is not kept with no end date.
who: anyone who owns one of those mobile numbers; the owner, whose live data fills with test gyms
how_often: every cloud phone test run (each release gate and each journeys or conditions run)
fix_line: Give tests a safe way to delete the gyms they made at the end of each run, sweep the ones already left, and switch test numbers to a range that cannot be a real mobile.

title: A gym cannot erase a member from the server, so a member's request to the gym to erase their details cannot be done
what: The privacy notice tells a member who left to ask the gym to erase the rest of their details. The server refuses to delete any member, plan, membership or receipt the gym typed in by hand; only imported ones and check-ins can be deleted, and even then the row keeps all its details with a deleted mark. A member who leaves the app keeps their name, join date and leave date in the gym's app list for good; only the mobile number is cleared. Their shop orders keep their name too. Nothing in these files removes any of these rows while the gym stays on MettleUp. HQ has no erase tool either (written down separately).
expected: The gym (or MettleUp on its behalf) can really erase one member's details on request, and a deleted record keeps no personal details.
who: members who ask their gym to erase their details
how_often: every erase request a gym gets
fix_line: Add an owner-only erase-member action that blanks the member's details in every gym table, and blank the details whenever a record is deleted.

title: Workout offer dates and the list of who joined are only deleted when the owner opens the offers page
what: The privacy notice promises workout offer dates go 90 days after the offer ends, and the record of who joined and left goes 1 year after. The deleting only runs when the owner opens the workout offer page or saves an offer. The nightly clean-up does not touch these. A gym that stops using offers keeps every member's counted workout dates and offer history with no end.
expected: Offer dates and the joined list are deleted on a schedule at the promised time, whoever opens the app.
who: members who joined a workout offer
how_often: every gym that stops opening its offers page
fix_line: Run the offer clean-up for every gym in the nightly job.

title: When a member joins a gym, the server keeps no record that they agreed to the notice or said they are 18 or over
what: The privacy notice says a member first ticks that they are 18 or older and agrees to the notice and terms before joining. The join on the server takes only the gym code, a name and an optional number; it keeps no record of the tick, the notice version or the time. So MettleUp cannot later show that a given member agreed, or to which version. The workout offer and the owner's terms both keep such a record; the member join does not.
expected: The join keeps when the member agreed, to which notice version, and that they said they are 18 or over, like the offer and the owner's terms do.
who: every member who joins a gym in the app
how_often: every join
fix_line: Send the notice version and the 18+ tick with the join and keep them with the member's row.

title: A removed staff member's name, mobile number and device sign-in history stay on the server for good
what: Removing a person from Staff and sign-in only marks them removed. Their name and mobile number stay. Every device sign-in they ever made also stays, with the device name and the times, even after it ends; nothing ever deletes these. The privacy notice says sign-in records are kept 7 days for now. Used sign-in codes are never deleted either.
expected: Ended sign-ins go after the period the notice states, and a removed person's mobile number is cleared after a stated time.
who: former owners and front-desk staff
how_often: every person removed, and every sign-in
fix_line: Add ended sign-ins and used codes to the nightly clean-up, and clear a removed person's mobile after a stated time.

title: The time limits the privacy notice gives for gym-shared data only run when someone opens that screen
what: The notice promises that leaderboard numbers go after 62 days, machine use after 63, workouts shared with gym mates after 60, the trainer summary after 90 days without an update, questions to a trainer after 180 days, and a sent workout report after 30. No timed job does any of this. Each clean-up runs only for one gym, and only when a member or staff person of that gym opens the matching screen. In a gym that stops using a feature, or stops using MettleUp, the data stays with no end. Machine use is also skipped while the gym is paused. Leaving the gym still deletes a member's rows at once, so this hits members who stay.
expected: Every time limit in the notice is kept by a nightly clean-up across all gyms, whether or not anyone opens a screen.
who: members of gyms that stop using a feature or MettleUp
how_often: every gym where nobody opens that screen for a while
fix_line: Add one nightly clean-up that applies every stated time limit to all gyms.

title: Numbers that started a free trial are kept in plain form for ever, even after the gym is deleted
what: When a gym is created with a WhatsApp-checked number, the number is saved in a list of numbers that already had a free trial. It is saved as the plain number, has no clean-up, and stays when the gym is deleted (only the link to the gym is cleared). The notice says WhatsApp number checks are kept for 2 days and that only a coded form of the number is kept. This part is not switched on live yet.
expected: The trial list keeps only a coded form of the number, and the notice states how long it is kept and why.
who: gym owners who start a gym with a checked number
how_often: every gym made that way, once switched on
fix_line: Store a coded form of the number and add the trial list, with its time, to the notice.

title: Deleting a member from the gym's list leaves their photo and body measurements behind, out of sight
what: The desk photo and the body measurements are saved under the member's id on the gym's list. When the gym deletes that member from its list, nothing removes them. The screens only open a listed member, so the gym no longer sees that they are still there. Only a whole gym delete removes them. The face photo and the body figures stay with no end date.
expected: Deleting a member from the gym's list also deletes their photo and measurements, or the gym is told what is kept and can remove it.
who: members a gym deletes from its list
how_often: every member deleted who had a photo or measurements
fix_line: When a member is deleted from the list, delete their photo and measurements too.

title: Door entry machines are not in the privacy notice, and every door punch is kept for ever
what: The door machine part (fingerprint, face or card machines at the gym door) records every punch with the member, the time and how they were checked, and keeps each one with no end date. The privacy notice describes check-ins only as scanning the QR poster and never mentions door machines or how long punches are kept. This part is not switched on live yet.
expected: Before door machines go live, the notice names them, says what each punch records and how long it is kept, and old punches are cleaned up.
who: members of gyms that add a door machine
how_often: every punch, once switched on
fix_line: Add door machines to the notice and give punches a clean-up time.

title: Records of what a gym paid MettleUp are erased when the gym is deleted, though the notice says they are kept as tax law needs
what: The notice says payments to MettleUp are kept as long as tax law requires. The new payment list and the payment record both go automatically the moment the gym is deleted, so a gym that leaves takes MettleUp's own proof of income with it. This part is not switched on live yet.
expected: Payment records to MettleUp outlive the gym for the time tax law requires, with the gym's other data removed.
who: MettleUp, at a tax check
how_often: every gym delete after paying
fix_line: Keep the payment records when a gym is deleted, without the link to the deleted gym.

title: Trainers now get a year of a member's workouts, but the privacy notice still says 30 workouts from 3 months
what: Since 14 Nov the member's phone shares up to 400 workouts from the last 12 months with the gym's trainers, with the best weight, reps and sets of up to 20 exercises each. The privacy notice tells members the trainer summary holds up to 30 workouts from the last 3 months. Members agree to a much smaller share than the one that really happens, and the sharing is on by default when they join.
expected: The privacy notice (English and Hindi) says what trainers really get: up to 12 months of workouts, with what each one holds.
who: members of every gym
how_often: every member with trainer sharing on
fix_line: Update the trainer summary line in the privacy notice to 12 months and up to 400 workouts, in both languages.

title: The privacy notice says nothing about the join-online form or the gym's web page, which collect names, numbers and questions
what: People who are not yet members can fill the gym's join-online form (name, mobile, gender, plan, a health tick) or ask the gym a question from its web page (name, mobile, question), and later chat with the page's AI helper. Their details go into the gym's enquiry list, and MettleUp also keeps its own copy of the mobile number. The page asks them to tick a consent, but the privacy notice lists only MettleUp's own demo form and the friend invite page. Nothing tells these people what is kept, for how long, or which outside AI reads a chat.
expected: The privacy notice has a part for the join-online form and the gym's web page: what is collected, that it goes to that gym, what MettleUp keeps itself and for how long, and which AI company reads chats.
who: people who join online or ask a gym from its web page
how_often: every join-online form and web page question
fix_line: Add a section on the join-online form and the gym web page to the privacy notice before these parts go further.

title: Mobile numbers from the join form and web page questions are kept for ever, only to count one day's tries
what: Every join-online form and every web page question also writes the person's mobile number into a MettleUp table used only to stop more than 3 tries a day. Nothing ever deletes those rows: they stay after the day is over, after the person asks to be erased, and after they become a member or leave. They go only when the whole gym is deleted.
expected: These spam-check rows are deleted after a day or two, as the WhatsApp number checks are.
who: people who join online or ask a gym from its web page
how_often: every form sent
fix_line: Delete these rows once they are older than 2 days, in the same nightly clean-up as the WhatsApp checks.

title: The direct-read record would keep the full query text, with any names or numbers in it, for 2 years and refuse every erase
what: The planned record of direct database looks (not live yet) saves each look's query text, up to 2,000 characters, for 2 years. A look like 'find the member with this mobile' keeps that mobile number and any name typed. The table refuses every delete younger than 2 years, so erasing a member or deleting a gym cannot remove it.
expected: The record keeps who looked, when and which tables and gyms, with names, numbers and other values in the query blanked out before saving.
who: members and gym staff whose details are looked up directly
how_often: every direct look, once the record is live
fix_line: Blank out quoted values and numbers in the query text before it is saved.

title: The direct-read record stops writing looks after 20,000 in all, though owners are told every look is recorded
what: The planned record of direct database looks keeps at most 2,000 looks a day and 20,000 in total. Past either number a look only adds to a hidden counter: the owner's list does not show it and no gap row is written. One busy session in the database dashboard can make thousands of looks, so the cap can be reached long before the 2 years run out.
expected: No look is dropped silently: either keep them all, or write a visible 'not recorded from .. to ..' row the owner sees, as is done for log gaps.
who: gym owners
how_often: once the cap is reached
fix_line: Write a visible gap row when looks are dropped, and raise or remove the total cap.

title: The door machine link would send members' names and every door punch unencrypted, while the privacy notice says data travels encrypted
what: The planned link for gym door machines (fingerprint, face or card) must answer plain, unencrypted web calls, because many machines cannot do the secure kind. Over it go each member's number and door punch times from the machine, and the member's name from MettleUp to the machine when a member is added. Anyone on the gym's internet line or on the way could read or change them. The privacy notice says data travels encrypted. This link is written but not switched on yet.
expected: Before door machines go live, either only machines that can talk securely are allowed, or names are never sent over the plain link and the notice says plainly which door-machine data is not encrypted.
who: members of gyms that connect a door machine
how_often: every door punch and every member added, once switched on
fix_line: Decide before launch: allow only secure machines, or send numbers only (no names) and tell members in the notice.

title: Buying a MettleUp plan online sends the gym owner's name and mobile to a payment company the privacy notice does not name for this
what: When a gym owner buys a MettleUp plan online, the server makes a payment link with MettleUp's own Razorpay or Cashfree account and passes the owner's name and mobile number. The privacy notice lists payments to MettleUp only as UPI or bank references, and its list of outside companies names only the gym's own payment company for members paying their gym. Online buying is switched off and in test mode today.
expected: Before online buying is switched on, the notice (both languages) says that MettleUp's payment company gets the owner's name, mobile and the amount.
who: gym owners who buy a plan online
how_often: every online plan purchase, once switched on
fix_line: Add MettleUp's payment company for plan purchases to the notice before switching online buying on.

title: The nightly backup is a full readable copy of every gym, and a look at it is never recorded
what: Each night the server stores a full copy of all gym data (members, payments, check-ins, staff) in Cloudflare storage for 7 days, as it is, without its own lock. Anyone who can sign in to MettleUp's Cloudflare account can open it, and nothing records that look. Gym owners are told MettleUp support looks only in a recorded window and that every look is recorded. The copy also still holds a deleted gym for up to 7 days.
expected: Opening a backup copy is written down like any other look (or the copy is locked with a key kept apart), and the notice's "every look is recorded" covers it or says it does not.
who: every gym and its members
how_often: whenever someone opens a backup copy
fix_line: Lock the backup with a separate key and record each restore or download in the HQ log.

title: The privacy notice says MettleUp tells members and the Board about a data leak, but the leak plan leaves both to the gym and HQ cannot reach members
what: The notice tells members that if their data leaks, MettleUp tells them in the app or by message and reports to the Data Protection Board. The written leak plan says the gym tells the Board and the members, and MettleUp only tells the gym. HQ can send a note only to gym admin apps, not to members. So for data MettleUp itself holds (a member's own account and saved copy, feedback), nobody is set to tell the member or the Board.
expected: The notice and the leak plan say the same thing about who tells members and the Board, and MettleUp has a way to tell members directly for the data it holds itself.
who: members whose data leaks
how_often: only if a leak happens
fix_line: Align the leak plan with the notice and give HQ a way to message affected members.

title: A gym owner's spoken AI Assistant request can go to Sarvam, a company the privacy notice never names
what: When the owner speaks to the AI Assistant, the recording goes first to Sarvam (an Indian speech-to-text company) whenever Sarvam's key is saved on the server; Groq is only the second choice. The privacy notice, in English and Hindi, says spoken requests go to Groq and its list of outside companies has no Sarvam. The spoken request can hold member names, amounts and other gym details. Whether Sarvam's key is saved on the live server could not be checked.
expected: Every outside company that hears a spoken request is named in the privacy notice (both languages) before any recording is sent there, or the recording goes only to the company the notice names.
who: gym owners who speak to the AI Assistant, and the members they name
how_often: every spoken request while Sarvam's key is saved
fix_line: Add Sarvam to the privacy notice (both languages, company table too), or drop Sarvam and use Groq only.

title: Erasing your data or deleting your account leaves the watch's copy behind
what: The watch keeps its own small store: the last workout's name, the gym's colour, and a screen diary of about two workouts with the time of every screen event and whether a workout was open, so it shows when the member trained. Nothing on the phone or the watch ever clears it: 'Erase all data' and 'Delete my account' on the phone send the watch nothing, and the watch has no erase of its own. It goes only when the watch app is removed. The privacy notice does not mention the watch in its delete steps.
expected: Erasing data or deleting the account also clears what the watch app holds (or the delete steps say to remove the watch app too).
who: members with the watch app who erase their data or delete their account
how_often: every erase or account delete
fix_line: Have the phone's erase and account delete send the watch a clear message that wipes its stored workout and diary, or add 'remove the watch app' to the delete steps.

title: The gym-owner site, the member site and every gym web page load their letters from Google, but the privacy notice says our websites send nothing out
what: Each visit to gyms.mettleup.fit, mettleup.fit or a gym's own web page makes the visitor's browser fetch fonts from Google, so Google gets the visitor's internet address, browser and the page they came from. The privacy notice says our websites use no analytics, and its list of companies names Google only for sign-in, pop-ups, Play, the member-list import and old Drive backups. A visitor is never told. Under EU and UK rules, which the notice says it follows, sending the address to Google this way without telling people has been ruled unlawful.
expected: Website visitors are told every outside company their visit reaches, or the pages carry their own fonts so nothing goes to Google.
who: every visitor to the websites and gym web pages
how_often: every page visit
fix_line: Serve the fonts from our own site (no Google call), or name Google for website fonts in the privacy notice in both languages.

title: The delete-account page says nothing is on our server unless you used Continue with Google, but joining a gym or signing in with a phone number puts data there
what: The page Google Play links to for account deletion says you only have an account if you tapped Continue with Google, and that otherwise nothing is saved on our server and there is nothing to delete. The privacy notice repeats it for EU and UK readers. But a member who only joined a gym with its code has their name, leaderboard numbers, trainer summary, machine use and pop-up code on the server, and phone-number sign-in (added 15 Nov) does not need Google at all. The email route also only works from the Google email address, so such a member is told there is nothing to ask for and has no way to ask. The page was last changed on 10 Nov, before phone sign-in.
expected: The delete-account page and the privacy notice say what a member who never used Google still has on the server (through their gym), how to remove it (leave the gym, or email us with their mobile number), and accept a mobile number as well as a Google email.
who: members who joined a gym or signed in with their number but never used Google
how_often: every such member who reads the page
fix_line: Rewrite the opening of the delete-account page and the matching privacy line to cover gym members and phone sign-in, and let them ask by mobile number.

title: The bring-a-friend page takes a stranger's name and number with no link to the privacy notice and no age line
what: A member's invite link opens a page where the friend types their name, mobile number and best time to train. The page says only that the gym sees the number. It has no link to any privacy notice, does not say who runs the page, how long the details are kept or how to have them removed, and asks nothing about age. The join-online form, by contrast, has an 18-or-older tick and a privacy link. The friend has never agreed to anything with MettleUp or the gym.
expected: The friend page says in one line who gets the details, for what, for how long and how to remove them, links the privacy notice, and says the offer is for people 18 or over, as the join-online form does.
who: friends of members who open an invite link
how_often: every friend invite sent
fix_line: Add a short notice line, a privacy link and an 18-or-over line to the friend invite page.

title: The gym-owner home page says the import AI never sees member details, but it sees some of them
what: The Import members card carries a tag "AI never sees member details" (Hindi too). Names, addresses, mobiles, emails and ID numbers are hidden first, but for up to 5 rows the AI is sent each member's plan, fee paid, joining and expiry dates, gender, batch and trainer, and any other column the gym has (for example blood group or weight) unless it looks like a name or address. The privacy notice says this correctly; only the home page tag overclaims.
expected: The home page says what the privacy notice says: names, numbers, emails and addresses are hidden; plans, amounts and dates of a few sample rows are not.
who: gym owners reading the home page
how_often: every visit to the home page; every AI import
fix_line: Change the tag to "AI never sees names or numbers" in both languages.

title: The privacy notice says a web page may remember only your light or dark choice, but the gym page keeps your chat for 90 days on the device
what: The websites part of the notice says the pages use no cookies and may remember your light or dark choice on your device. The gym's web page keeps a visitor code and the last 40 lines of the chat with its helper in the browser for 90 days, and the join-online form keeps the name, mobile, gender and plan typed so far until the tab closes, and the chosen language. On a shared or family phone the next person can see that chat.
expected: The notice lists what each page keeps on the device and for how long (chat lines 90 days, the join form until the tab closes, language), or the gym page keeps less.
who: visitors who chat on a gym web page or start the join-online form
how_often: every chat on a gym web page, once that page is live
fix_line: Add one line to the websites part of the notice naming what pages keep on the device, in both languages.

title: The privacy notice changed three times after 10 Nov, but the apps told nobody
what: The notice promises that before a change that affects you, MettleUp tells you in the app. It changed on 12, 13 and 15 Nov (gym messages, the AI Assistant, sign-in with your phone number). The member app asks members to tick again only when its agreed version changes, and that version is still 10 Nov; the admin app's terms version is also 10 Nov. Nothing else in either app announces a notice change.
expected: Each change that affects people is announced in the app before it applies (a news line or a fresh tick), and the version numbers move with the notice.
who: members and gym owners
how_often: every change to the privacy notice
fix_line: Add a step to every notice change: raise the app version date or add a news line in both apps.

title: Plan-end reminders 7, 3 and 1 days before are promised for when online payments start, but nothing is built
what: The shipping and delivery page says that when online payments start, the admin app reminds the owner 7, 3 and 1 days before a monthly or yearly plan ends. The list of reminder days exists, but no screen or job reads it. When online payments are switched on, owners will get no reminder.
expected: The admin app shows the reminder on those days before online payments are switched on, or the page drops the promise.
who: gym owners on a monthly or yearly plan
how_often: every plan end, once online payments start
fix_line: Build the reminder card in the admin app and add it to the online-payments switch-on list.

title: The AI Assistant help says it writes a workout plan for free, then that saving it costs 3 credits
what: The help article says the AI can write a workout plan for a member "for free", and the next sentence says saving it uses 3 credits. A plan that is not saved is of no use, so in practice every AI plan costs 3 credits.
expected: The help says plainly that an AI workout plan costs 3 credits when you save it, and trying it costs nothing.
who: gym owners
how_often: every read of that help article
fix_line: Reword the line to "writes a workout plan for a member; you pay 3 credits only if you save it".

title: A plan HQ sets by hand can be switched back to Starter overnight by an older Starter payment
what: When a gym pays for Starter while Pro (or the free trial) is still running, the system plans a switch to Starter for later. If HQ then sets the gym's plan by hand (for example Pro yearly after a payment), that planned switch is not cleared. On the planned day the nightly job moves the gym to Starter anyway, although HQ set Pro. HQ never shows that a switch is planned.
expected: Setting the plan by hand should cancel any planned switch, or HQ should show the planned switch and ask before saving.
who: gym owners who paid for Pro
how_often: only when a Starter payment came in while Pro or the trial was running, then HQ set the plan by hand
fix_line: Clear the planned switch when HQ sets a plan, and show any planned switch on the gym's page

title: Confirming a Starter payment says the gym moves to Starter now, but it stays on Pro until its paid time or trial ends
what: Before Confirm, HQ says it sets Starter and, for a Pro gym, that it changes the gym from Pro to Starter. The server keeps the gym on Pro until the Pro time or the free trial ends and only then switches. After Confirm the gym's row and page read Pro, and nothing in HQ says a switch to Starter is coming or when.
expected: The words before Confirm and the gym's page should say the gym stays on Pro until a date and then moves to Starter.
who: MettleUp
how_often: every Starter payment from a gym on Pro or on its trial
fix_line: Send the planned switch to HQ and say it in the Confirm words and on the gym's page

title: HQ says every yearly or lifetime gym gets 100 free AI credits a month, but a Starter yearly gym gets 50
what: On a gym's AI credits card, when nothing has been used yet, HQ says the owner gets 100 free credits every month on a paid yearly or lifetime plan. The server and the price list give 50 a month on Starter yearly and 100 only on Pro. Someone at MettleUp reading this could promise an owner the wrong number.
expected: The line should say 50 on Starter yearly and 100 on Pro yearly or founding lifetime, or show the gym's own number that the server already sends.
who: MettleUp
how_often: every Starter yearly gym that has not used AI credits yet
fix_line: Use the gym's own monthly free number in that line

title: HQ shows test-mode online payments as real money to refund
what: Online buying works only with the payment company's test keys today, and the Online payments to check card shows only when that test switch is on. Yet the card shows each one as money a gym paid (rupees, company, payment id) and asks HQ to refund it in the company's dashboard and mark it refunded. Nothing in HQ says test mode, and the plans those test payments make look like real paying gyms.
expected: While payments are in test mode, HQ should say so on the Payments page and on each online payment, and count test plans apart from real ones.
who: MettleUp
how_often: every online payment while payments are in test mode
fix_line: Show a test-mode line on the Payments page and mark each test payment

title: Money taken by hand for a plan or an AI credit pack keeps no amount and makes no receipt
what: When HQ sets a plan by hand after a payment, or adds an AI credit pack the gym paid for, only a free-text note is kept. No amount is stored and no MettleUp receipt is made, unlike a payment confirmed on the Payments page. MettleUp cannot add up what it was paid, and the owner has no receipt.
expected: A paid plan or pack added by hand should store the amount and make a receipt the owner can open, like a confirmed payment.
who: gym owners and MettleUp
how_often: every plan or credit pack set by hand after a payment
fix_line: Ask for the amount and write it to the payments ledger so a receipt is made

title: HQ cannot undo or record a refund for a payment that already became a plan
what: Once a payment is confirmed, or an online payment became a plan, HQ shows only the outcome. There is no way to undo a confirm made by mistake, or to record that a payment made twice or above the price was paid back. The paid time and the receipt stay as they are. The refunds page promises to refund money paid twice by mistake or above the price.
expected: HQ should be able to mark a confirmed or online payment as refunded, with the amount, and take back the paid time it gave, so the plan and receipt match the money kept.
who: gym owners who paid twice or too much, and MettleUp
how_often: every refund or wrong confirm
fix_line: Add a refund mark for applied payments that stores the amount and pulls back the paid time

title: Any lifetime plan HQ sets, also Starter or on a test gym, quietly uses one of the 25 founding places
what: The founding offer (Pro for life, first 25 gyms) counts every gym on a lifetime plan, whatever the plan and whether it is a test or demo gym. HQ's plan picker offers lifetime for Starter as well as Pro and gives no warning that each one uses a founding place. HQ never shows how many founding places are left.
expected: Only real founding gyms should count, and HQ should show the places left and warn before a lifetime plan uses one.
who: gym owners hoping for a founding place
how_often: every lifetime plan set by hand
fix_line: Count only founding payments, or Pro lifetime on real gyms, and show the count in HQ

title: Making the free trial longer for a gym that already paid gives it no extra free days
what: A gym that pays during its free trial gets its paid time added after the trial's end on that day. If HQ later makes the trial longer, the paid time does not move, so the new free days fall inside time the gym already paid for. HQ says the trial now ends later, as if the gym gained something.
expected: Moving the trial end of a gym that already paid should move its paid time too, or HQ should say the extra days give nothing.
who: gym owners who paid during the trial
how_often: only when HQ lengthens the trial of a gym that already paid
fix_line: Warn in the trial box when the gym already has paid time

title: The admin app never shows what a pack of AI credits costs, so an owner asks MettleUp for credits without knowing the price
what: The AI credits sheet only says to write to MettleUp in Help and feedback and say how many credits you want. It shows no pack and no price, although the server already sends the three packs and their rupee prices to the app, and the website notes say the prices are shown in the app when an owner needs more. The only place the prices are written is the website's About page.
expected: When an owner runs low, the sheet shows the three packs and what each costs (50 for 149 rupees, 150 for 399, 500 for 999), with the same Ask MettleUp button.
who: owners
how_often: every time an owner wants more credits
fix_line: Show the three packs and their prices on the credits sheet, next to Ask MettleUp for credits

title: The server takes whatever number of credits the admin app says a task costs
what: When an owner confirms a task, the admin app works out the price itself (1 for a message or a save, 3 for a workout plan) and sends that number. The server checks only that it is between 1 and 9 and that the gym has that many; it never works it out again from the task it saved. An admin app that is old or changed in the browser could save a workout plan for 1 credit.
expected: The server works out the price from the actions saved with the task, and takes exactly that.
who: MettleUp
how_often: only with an old or altered admin app
fix_line: Let the server count the price from the saved task's actions instead of trusting the number sent

title: The AI credits sheet's price list leaves out renewals, extensions, enquiries and expenses
