what: Under What uses credits the sheet lists only a message sent and a member or payment saved for 1 credit. Renewing a plan, extending a plan, saving an enquiry and saving an expense also take 1 credit each, and the website's table names enquiries and expenses.
expected: The sheet names every task that takes a credit, in the same words as the website.
who: owners
how_often: every time the sheet is opened
fix_line: Change the row to name every saved task that costs 1 credit

title: Every gym gets 20 starter credits, but the website says only the free trial gets them and a monthly plan gets none
what: The server adds 20 starter credits the first time an owner opens the assistant, trial or not, so a gym already on a monthly plan also gets them. The website's table says the free trial gets 20 once and a monthly plan gets none.
expected: The website and the server agree on who gets the 20 starter credits.
who: owners
how_often: once per gym
fix_line: Say on the website that every gym gets 20 starter credits once, or give them only in the trial

title: Record a payment from the assistant fails for a member who owes on two plans
what: The Record a payment button under a member's dues asks to record the whole amount owed across all their plans. The draft puts that money against the oldest unpaid plan only and has no way to pick a plan, so the check refuses it: they owe less for this plan, type that or less. The owner has to lower the amount and do it a second time.
expected: Record a payment for a member with two unpaid plans either splits the money over the plans or lets the owner pick the plan, so one tap can finish.
who: owners
how_often: when a member owes on more than one plan
fix_line: Prefill only the oldest plan's due, or add a plan choice to the payment card

title: Cash taken offline that the server later refused disappears from the member's dues and the money counts
what: When a payment taken with no internet is refused once it is sent, it is kept only in the warning bar at the top. The member's page goes back to showing the full amount still owed, the 'payment still being sent' block no longer stops a second payment, the Today line of money waiting to send leaves it out, and the clear-offline-copy warning does not name it as money. The member already paid and holds a printed receipt.
expected: Money taken and printed for stays visible on the member's page as taken but not yet saved, blocks a second payment for the same plan, and is named with its amount in every count and warning until the owner settles it.
who: members and front desk
how_often: whenever an offline payment is refused, rare
fix_line: Show refused money on the member's page as taken but not saved, and count it in the waiting money and the clear warning

title: An owner can wipe a refused receipt that was already printed, leaving no record of the cash and a gap in the receipt numbers
what: For a refused offline payment the owner gets 'Remove from this device'. The confirm says only that it was never sent and will be gone. It does not say it is a receipt the member already holds or how much money it was. After removing, the cash has no record anywhere and that receipt number is simply missing, although the rest of the app keeps every cancelled receipt so the numbers never have a gap.
expected: A refused receipt can only be saved as a cancelled receipt with a reason, or the confirm names the amount and the receipt number and warns that the number will be missing from the receipt book.
who: owners
how_often: rare, only after a refused offline payment
fix_line: Offer only Save as cancelled receipt for refused money, or name the amount and number in the confirm

title: A plan and payment for a new member the server refused are sent anyway after 30 days, making a receipt for nobody
what: When a new member added offline is refused, the plan sold and payment taken with them wait on the device. After 30 days the refused member is deleted from the device for privacy, but the plan and payment stay, and on the next send they go to the gym's records. The server does not check that the member exists, so the gym's money totals get a receipt and a plan that belong to no member, and no member page shows them.
expected: When a refused new member is removed, the plan and payment that wait with them are kept back for the owner to settle (save as cancelled, or attach to a real member), never sent on their own.
who: owners
how_often: rare, a refused offline new member left 30 days
fix_line: Hold the waiting plan and payment with the member, and ask the owner before the member is removed

title: When the app cannot close a member's open payment link, the desk payment is saved anyway and the link can still be paid
what: Before saving cash or UPI on Collect payment, the app asks the server to close any open online payment link for that due. If that ask fails (no internet, the server or payment company does not answer), the app carries on, saves the desk payment and says nothing. The link the member already has stays open, so they can pay the same due a second time. Today payment links are test mode only, so no real money moves yet; it bites once live payments are switched on.
expected: If the open links could not be closed, the desk is told that a payment link for this due may still be open and is asked to cancel it or tell the member not to pay it, before or right after the cash is saved.
who: members, desk
how_often: each desk payment made while the link check fails and a link is open
fix_line: When the link check fails, warn the desk on the sheet and keep the warning on the member's page until the link is closed

title: Cancelling a receipt that was paid online does not give the member's money back, and the sheet never says so
what: The cancel-receipt sheet says the receipt stops counting as money received and the amount goes back onto the member's dues. For a receipt the member paid online through Razorpay or Cashfree, the money is still with the gym's payment company: nothing refunds it, and the sheet gives no hint to refund it there. The panel has no refund record at all; a refund and a typing mistake look the same apart from the typed reason. The member can then be chased for money they already paid.
expected: When the receipt was paid online, the sheet says the money stays with the payment company and asks whether it was refunded there, and the cancelled receipt shows whether money went back.
who: owners, members
how_often: each cancelled receipt that was paid online
fix_line: Say on the cancel sheet when a receipt was paid online and record whether the money was refunded

title: After free days are added and then the start date is changed, the receipt shows the free days as paid
what: A plan that has not started can get free days (freeze or gift) and then have its start date changed. The start change keeps the day count, so the free days move with it, but the receipt reads the free-day note against the old end date, no longer matches, and falls back to printing the whole new period as what was paid, with no free-days line.
expected: The receipt keeps showing the paid period and the free days on their own line after a start date change.
who: members
how_often: rare: free days given before the plan starts, then the start moved
fix_line: Move the free-day note dates with the start change, or read the receipt's paid dates from the sale

title: The pass box says no plan and no dues, but a member switched to a pass keeps their old plan and any money they still owe
what: Ticking Comes with a pass shows the hint that the member has no plan and no dues. For an existing member, their earlier plan and any unpaid balance stay and still count in the dues total and on the Collect payment sheet. Only the renewal list leaves them out.
expected: The hint says that old plans and unpaid dues stay as they are, or the sheet shows what the member still owes when the box is ticked.
who: owners, desk
how_often: each time an existing member with dues is switched to a pass
fix_line: Change the hint to say old dues stay, and show the amount when there is one

title: A GST-registered gym's monthly profit counts the GST it owes the government as its own money
what: Every fee is stored as the full amount the member paid, with the GST inside it. The monthly Collection and Profit on the Expenses page add those full amounts and take away only the spending. For a gym with a GST number, about 5 rupees in every 105 collected is tax the gym must pay over, but the page shows it as profit, with no word that tax is inside.
expected: For a gym with a GST number, profit is shown before tax (or the page says plainly that GST is still inside the number).
who: owners of gyms with a GST number
how_often: every month
fix_line: Take the GST out of fees received by a registered gym before working out profit, or label the number as including GST

title: Money collected on Your growth is smaller than Collected on Expenses for the same month when the gym runs a shop
what: Your growth counts only fee receipts as Money collected. The Expenses page counts fees plus shop orders handed over as Collected. A gym with a shop sees two different collected amounts for the same month, and Your growth does not say shop sales are left out.
expected: The same month shows the same collected amount everywhere, or each page names what it counts (fees only, or fees and shop).
who: owners of gyms with a shop
how_often: every month with a shop sale
fix_line: Call the growth line Fees collected, or add shop sales to it the way Expenses does

title: Past pass visits change company or disappear when a member's pass box is changed
what: A check-in by the gym's QR in the member app is saved without a pass company. The monthly pass count gives it to whatever company the member has today. If the desk unticks the pass box, every past QR visit of that member drops out of the old months. If the desk changes FITPASS to cultpass, all the old QR visits move to cultpass. If the box is ticked again later, the start day resets to today and the earlier QR visits stay uncounted. Desk check-ins keep their company, so the two kinds of visit drift apart. The owner matches the pass company's payment against a count that can change after the month is closed.
expected: Every pass visit keeps the company it was made under, so a past month's count never changes when the member's details change.
who: owners
how_often: each time a pass member's pass box is changed
fix_line: Save the pass company on each visit when it is made, the QR check-in included

title: Every receipt for a plan says it includes the joining fee, even a small later part payment
what: When a plan has a joining fee, each receipt against that plan prints the line that it includes a one-time joining fee of that amount. A member paying in parts gets the same line on the second and third receipt too, and on a receipt smaller than the fee itself. An accountant reading the receipts would count the joining fee more than once.
expected: The joining fee line shows only on the receipt that took it, or reads as the plan's fee, not as part of this payment.
who: members, owners
how_often: every part payment on a plan with a joining fee
fix_line: Word the line as the plan's joining fee, or print it on the first receipt only

title: A new branch gets the first branch's paid plan, paid-until date and founding Pro for life free
what: When an owner adds a branch, the new branch is given the first branch's MettleUp plan, billing and paid-until date. A gym that has paid for a year gets the new branch paid for the same year without paying for it. A founding gym (Pro for life, one branch) gets Pro for life on every new branch, cannot be asked to pay for it, and each branch also takes one of the 25 founding places. The add-branch sheet only speaks of the free trial.
expected: A new branch shares only the free trial. After the trial it pays its own price (half price, as the website says), and the founding offer covers one branch and uses one place.
who: owners of paid or founding gyms who add a branch; MettleUp loses the branch fee
how_often: every branch added after the gym has paid
fix_line: Copy only the trial dates to a new branch; give it its own unpaid plan, and keep the founding offer to the first branch

title: An extra branch is charged full price, but the website promises half price
what: The website and the About page say each extra branch pays half price. When a branch buys or renews its MettleUp plan, the price is worked out from the plan and monthly or yearly only, so a second or third branch is asked for the full price.
expected: A branch other than the first is asked for half the plan price, as the website says.
who: owners with more than one branch
how_often: every payment by an extra branch
fix_line: Halve the price for any branch that is not the group's first, or change the website wording

title: After live payments start, an old test connection still shows Connected and payment links quietly fail
what: A gym that connected Razorpay or Cashfree during test mode keeps a green Connected badge once MettleUp switches live payments on, and the Test mode label disappears. The server no longer makes links with a test connection, so the desk taps Make a payment link and only reads that the link could not be made, try again. Nothing tells the owner to connect again with live keys, and Paste keys is hidden while it shows Connected.
expected: The test connection is shown as needing live keys, with the paste-keys button, and the desk is told why no link can be made.
who: owners and desk staff of gyms that connected a company in test mode
how_often: every payment link, from the day live payments start
fix_line: Show a test-mode connection as needing live keys once payments are live, and say so on the desk sheet

title: The key help always tells the owner to use test keys, also when payments are live
what: When the owner opens Paste keys, the help line says to make a test key (Razorpay) or use the test keys (Cashfree), whether payments are in test mode or live. Once live, a test key is refused with a different message, so the owner is told two opposite things.
expected: In live mode the help asks for the live keys; in test mode it asks for test keys.
who: owners connecting a payment company
how_often: every connect after live payments start
fix_line: Pick the help line by test or live mode

title: A member who paid twice shows as more than due, with an I saved it button and no word about a refund
what: If the desk takes cash for a due and the member then pays an old online link, the payment comes in late and lands on Today under Paid online, receipt not made, as more than what is due. The card asks the desk to save it by hand and tap I saved it. It does not say the member has paid twice and is owed money back, although the app knows the link was paid after it was closed.
expected: The card says the member paid twice, shows both payments and asks the desk to refund one at the payment company.
who: members who pay twice; desk staff
how_often: each late payment of a closed link after the desk took the money
fix_line: Use the late flag to name it a double payment and ask for a refund instead of I saved it

title: A refund made at the payment company after the receipt is saved never reaches the admin app
what: The app asks the payment company about a refund only before it makes the receipt. If the owner later refunds the payment in Razorpay or Cashfree, the receipt stays, and the money keeps counting as collected on Today and in the reports until someone voids it by hand. Nothing reminds them.
expected: A refund found later is shown on Today so the desk can void the receipt.
who: owners who refund an online payment
how_often: each refund after the receipt was made
fix_line: Look for refunds on paid links for some days after the receipt and list them on Today

title: A cancelled payment link leaves no button to make a new one
what: When a payment link on the sheet ends as cancelled, the desk reads This link was cancelled and sees no button. A link that ran out gets a Make a payment link button; a cancelled one does not, so the desk must close and reopen the sheet.
expected: The same Make a payment link button as for a link that ran out.
who: desk staff
how_often: rare
fix_line: Show the make-a-link button for a cancelled link too

title: A person who paid online when joining still shows "Not paid yet" on Enquiries, and Add as member there lets the desk charge them again
what: On the Enquiries page, every online join request says "Not paid yet.", because the gym server always saves it as unpaid; the real online payment is kept elsewhere. Add as member on that page opens Sell membership with the whole fee due, does not close the person's open payment link, and gives no warning. Only Today's Joined online card checks the payment and offers Approve. So the desk can take the fee in cash from someone who already paid online, and the person can still pay online after paying at the desk. The money check later says "They may have paid twice".
expected: The Enquiries row says Paid online when the payment company confirmed it, and Add as member on a join request does what Today's card does: close open payment links first, and send a paid request to Approve instead of a second sale.
who: owners, front desk and members who join online
how_often: every online join paid online that the desk opens from Enquiries instead of Today
fix_line: Read the join payment on the Enquiries row and route Add as member through the same checks as Today's card

title: A person who asked to join online at one price is sold the plan at today's price when the desk taps Make member
what: The join request row shows the price the person saw and agreed to on the join page. When the desk taps Make member (from Today or Enquiries), Sell membership opens on that plan but fills in the plan's current price, not the agreed one. If the owner changed the price in between, the member is charged a different amount with no warning. Approve after an online payment does use the agreed price, so the two ways disagree.
expected: Make member opens Sell membership with the price and joining fee the person agreed to on the join page, or says plainly that the price has changed since.
who: members who join online, front desk
how_often: only when a plan price changes between the request and Make member
fix_line: Pass the agreed price and joining fee into Sell membership, or warn when they differ

title: Cancelling a receipt the member paid online says nothing about giving the money back
what: Cancel receipt on a member page says only that the receipt will no longer count as money received and the amount goes back on their dues. For a fee the member paid online through the gym's payment company, the money is still in the gym's account, and nothing tells the owner to refund it there. The member then shows as owing a fee they already paid, and the money check treats that payment as already saved, so it never comes up again.
expected: For a receipt paid online, the cancel sheet says the money stays with the gym until it is refunded at the payment company, so the owner refunds it or keeps the receipt.
who: owners and members who paid online
how_often: each time an owner cancels a receipt that was paid online
fix_line: Add one line to the cancel sheet for online-paid receipts saying to refund at the payment company

title: The Plan ending WhatsApp asks the member to pay for a plan the gym no longer sells
what: The ready-typed Plan ending and Plan ended messages on a member page give the renewal price and a UPI pay link for the member's current plan. They use that plan even after the owner switched it off. The desk cannot sell a switched-off plan, so the member is asked to pay an amount the desk will not accept for that plan.
expected: When the member's plan is no longer sold, the message leaves out the price and pay link, or uses the plan the desk would sell instead.
who: owners and members
how_often: for members whose plan was switched off
fix_line: Skip the renewal amount when the member's plan is no longer active

title: An owner who paid MettleUp by UPI or bank transfer can never open the receipt for it
what: When MettleUp confirms a UPI or bank payment, the server makes a numbered receipt for it. The only list that shows these receipts sits inside the Pay online part of the Pay MettleUp screen, and that part asks the server nothing while online paying is switched off, which it is. So the owner sees Confirmed, paid until a date, but no receipt anywhere. The receipt page itself tells them to open it from Your receipts, which they cannot see.
expected: Every confirmed payment shows its receipt on Pay MettleUp, whether online paying is on or off.
who: owners
how_often: every time
fix_line: Show the gym's receipts list on Pay MettleUp even while online paying is off

title: An owner who reports paying MettleUp more or less than the price gets no word, and the extra is never marked to be paid back
what: The amount box on Pay MettleUp can be changed to anything. The screen sends it without saying it differs from the price. On HQ only a short amount gets a warning; an amount above the price is confirmed as is, the receipt shows the full amount, and nothing records that the extra is owed back, though the refunds page promises to refund it.
expected: The owner is told when the amount differs from the price, and an over-payment is marked in HQ as extra to refund.
who: owners
how_often: sometimes
fix_line: Warn the owner before sending a different amount, and flag an over-payment in HQ as extra to refund

title: The WhatsApp receipt and the printed receipt can show different amounts still due
what: The printed receipt shows what is still owed on that one membership. The WhatsApp receipt sent from the same screen says the member's whole amount owed across every membership is still due, with a pay link for it. A member with a second unpaid plan or PT pack gets one figure on paper and a bigger one on WhatsApp.
expected: Both copies of one receipt name the same amount still due, or say clearly which plans it covers.
who: members
how_often: sometimes
fix_line: Use the same still-due amount on the printed and WhatsApp receipt

title: Adding a GST number quietly turns every plan price into a price that already includes GST
what: Settings says only that the GST number shows on receipts. Once it is saved, every receipt treats the amount paid as including GST and splits it into a smaller taxable value plus CGST and SGST. Nothing on Settings or the Plans price box says prices now include GST, so an owner who expects GST to be added on top finds less income on paper than planned.
expected: Settings and the plan price box say that with a GST number every price includes GST, and at what rate.
who: owners
how_often: every time
fix_line: Say on the GST box and the price box that prices include GST once a GST number is saved

title: A shop order the member already paid online looks unpaid on the Shop page, and Collected says the money was just taken
what: When a member pays for a shop order in the app, the server keeps a list of shop orders paid online so the Shop page can say Paid online. Nothing in the admin app reads that list, and the paid-online sweep skips shop payments. The order card looks exactly like an unpaid one and still offers the pay-by-QR or link box. Once the payment is marked paid, the check before Collected only warns about a payment found paid at that very moment, so tapping Collected (paid) shows Order N collected, Rs X taken. The desk can take cash for an order that was already paid.
expected: An order paid online shows Paid online with the amount, hides the pay box, and Collected says it was paid online instead of asking for money.
who: members, desk staff
how_often: every shop order paid in the member app
fix_line: Show the paid-online mark on each order card and use it when the desk taps Collected

title: A shop order paid online can be cancelled, by the gym or the member, and nobody is told to give the money back
what: The gym's Cancel order sheet says the items go back into stock and the member sees Cancelled. It never checks whether the member already paid online and says nothing about a refund. The member can also cancel their own order in the app while it is new, even after paying. Cancelling does not close the order's open payment link either, so a saved link can still be paid for a cancelled order. The money stays with the gym's payment company with no record that it is owed back.
expected: Cancelling an order that was paid online says so, tells the owner to refund it at the payment company, and closes any open link; the member cannot cancel a paid order alone.
who: members, owners
how_often: each time a paid shop order is cancelled
fix_line: Check for an online payment before cancelling, close open links, and say the money must be refunded

title: While payments are in test mode, a test payment for a shop order makes the desk hand over the goods for free
what: The server's own rule says a test-mode payment must never let the desk hand over shop goods. But the check the desk runs before Collected counts any link found paid, test or live. A member who pays a shop order on a test payment page (anyone can) makes the desk read that the member has just paid Rs X online, do not take money, tap Collected again to hand it over. The words never say test mode. The gym gives the goods and no money ever arrives.
expected: A test-mode payment is never treated as money: the desk is told it was a test and takes the money as usual.
who: owners, desk staff
how_often: every shop order paid on a test payment page while test mode is on
fix_line: Leave test-mode payments out of the check before Collected, or say plainly that it was a test

title: Once paying online when joining is switched on, the invite screen and printed join poster still say pay at the desk
what: The WhatsApp message with the join link stops saying You pay at the gym desk once online paying on joining is on. The invite screen's explanation under the link and the printed Become a member poster always say they pay at the desk. When that switch is turned on, the owner and new people read two different things about where to pay. The switch is off today.
expected: The screen text and the poster follow the same switch as the WhatsApp message.
who: owners, new people joining online
how_often: once online paying on joining is switched on
fix_line: Make the screen text and the poster steps depend on the same switch

title: After paying MettleUp online, the owner comes back to a screen that says nothing about whether the payment worked
what: The payment company sends the owner back to the Pay MettleUp screen with no sign of how the payment went. The screen reads the plan once when it opens and never again, so if the payment takes a few seconds to land, or failed, or was left half way, the owner sees the old plan and the same buy buttons, with no word of paid, failed or being checked. The card promises the plan changes within seconds. A worried owner may tap another plan and pay a second time, because only the very same purchase reuses the earlier payment page.
expected: Coming back from the payment page, the owner sees paid, still being checked, or did not go through, and the screen updates by itself when the payment lands.
who: owners
how_often: every online payment, once online paying is switched on
fix_line: Read the payment result on return, show it in words, and re-check the plan for a minute after

title: The Pay online card never says payments are not refunded, even for the Rs 29,999 founding payment
what: The refund page and the terms say that once a paid plan is on, payments are not refunded. The Pay online card shows the buy buttons, including Pro for life at Rs 29,999, with no word about refunds and no link to the refund rules. Only a Starter bought while Pro is running gets a line about no money back for the days left.
expected: Next to the buy buttons, one plain line that payments are not refunded (except a double payment or paying too much), with a link to the refund page.
who: owners
how_often: every online payment, once online paying is switched on
fix_line: Add a no-refund line and the refund page link to the Pay online card

title: A member who already paid for MettleUp Plus can be shown the buy buttons again and charged a second time
what: The app decides whether to show the buy buttons only from what it remembers on the phone. After Erase all data it forgets the purchase and only asks Google Play again the next time the app is started fresh; the same happens when Google Play did not answer at start. In that gap the member sees the monthly, yearly and for-life buttons again. A member with the for-life plan who taps monthly, or a monthly member who taps for life, is charged again by Google Play, and nothing warns them. A monthly member who taps yearly is told Thank you and the app then says they pay every year, while Google Play keeps charging every month.
expected: Before showing the buy buttons, the app asks Google Play what this account already owns; a member who already owns Plus is told so and is never offered a second plan, and a tap that Google Play answers with already owned keeps the plan they really have.
who: members who bought MettleUp Plus
how_often: rare: after Erase all data, or when Google Play did not answer at app start; nobody today because buying is switched off
fix_line: Ask Google Play what the account owns each time the Plus screen opens and hide the buy buttons for an owner; on already owned, keep the plan Google Play has, not the one tapped

title: Someone who stops working at a gym keeps every paid feature free for good
what: Once a person proves with the admin-app PIN that they are a gym owner or desk staff, the phone remembers it and gives every MettleUp Plus feature free. Nothing ever checks again: if the owner removes them as staff, or the gym leaves MettleUp, the phone still says You work at that gym and keeps everything open until the app data is erased. The gym-member unlock, by contrast, follows the gym's list and ends 7 days after the plan ends.
expected: The staff unlock is checked again from time to time, like the gym-member unlock, and ends when the person is no longer staff at a MettleUp gym.
who: former desk staff and owners
how_often: every time someone leaves a gym's staff, once Plus is switched on
fix_line: Re-check the staff proof with the server once a launch and drop the unlock when it no longer holds

title: When the connection drops during a Plus payment, the app says nothing was charged and does not check again
what: Every Google Play answer other than paid, waiting, cancelled or store-not-reachable is treated as a failed payment, including a network drop in the middle of paying. The member then reads that the payment did not go through and nothing was charged, and the app does not ask Google Play what the member now owns. If Google Play did take the money, Plus stays locked until the app is started fresh or the member taps I already paid. Buying is not switched on yet, so nobody meets this today.
expected: After an unclear answer from Google Play, the app asks Google Play again what the member owns before saying anything about money, and says it is checking rather than that nothing was charged.
who: members buying MettleUp Plus
how_often: rare: only when the connection drops while paying, once payments are live
fix_line: Ask Google Play again after any unclear answer and change the words to say the app is checking

title: A waiting Plus payment that Google approves while the app is closed is refunded and taken back if the app is not opened within 3 days
what: Google Play refunds any purchase the app does not confirm within 3 days. The app confirms a purchase only from the phone, either while it is open or the next time it starts fresh. A member who paid by a slow method, closed the app and does not open it for 3 days after Google approves gets the money back automatically and loses Plus without being told why. No server confirms purchases instead.
expected: Purchases are confirmed with Google by MettleUp's server as soon as Google approves them, so a closed app never lets a paid plan lapse.
who: members who pay for Plus by a slow method
how_often: rare, once payments are live
fix_line: Have the server confirm each Plus purchase with Google, together with the server purchase check

title: Once MettleUp Plus is switched on, a gym owner, trainer or desk person found by phone number keeps every paid feature free for ever, even after leaving the gym
what: When the phone number sign-in finds someone as a gym's owner, trainer or desk staff, the app notes them as gym staff the moment they tap Join, and that note is never checked again. It is only removed if they erase all data. Someone who stops working at the gym, or never finishes joining, keeps every paid feature free. The server's search only leaves out suspended gyms. Plus is switched off today, so nobody is affected yet.
expected: The free unlock for gym staff should last only while the person is still on that gym's staff and the gym still uses MettleUp, and the app should check this again from time to time, as it already does for members' gym plans.
who: MettleUp (lost Plus sales), gym staff
how_often: once Plus is on, every staff member who leaves a gym
fix_line: Check the staff unlock again against the server from time to time, and drop it when the person is no longer on that gym's staff

title: Phone number sign-in tells trainers they get every MettleUp feature free, but the Plus page says only owners and desk staff do
what: When the phone number sign-in finds a trainer, it shows 'As a trainer, you get every MettleUp feature free' and unlocks Plus for them. The Plus page and the plan rules name only gym owners and desk staff, and the other staff route needs an admin PIN.
expected: One rule for who on a gym's staff gets Plus free, with the same words on the sign-in card and the Plus page.
who: trainers, members reading the Plus page
how_often: every trainer found by phone number once Plus is on
fix_line: Decide if trainers count as staff for Plus, then make the sign-in card and the Plus page say the same

title: A member who pays for MettleUp Plus and then joins a gym or works at one is never told the Google Play plan keeps charging
what: When a member who bought the monthly or yearly MettleUp Plus later joins a gym that uses MettleUp (or is added as desk staff), the app switches them to free through the gym. The MettleUp Plus page then only says the gym gives every feature free and hides the part about what they bought. Nothing says their Google Play plan is still running and still charged every month or year, for features they now get free.
expected: When a member has a running paid plan and also gets everything free through a gym or staff role, the MettleUp Plus page says so and tells them they can cancel the paid plan in Google Play.
who: paying Plus members who later join a MettleUp gym
how_often: every renewal after they join, once payments are live
fix_line: Show a line on the Plus page when a paid plan runs while the gym already makes it free

title: A Plus payment that is waiting, or a plan that is cancelled or refunded, is only noticed when the app is fully restarted
what: When Google Play says a payment is waiting, the app tells the member that Plus opens when Google Play confirms it. But when Google Play confirms later, the phone part that hears it no longer has anyone to tell, so the app does not open Plus. The app only asks Google Play what the member owns once, when it starts fresh; coming back to the app does not ask again. So a member who paid by a slow method waits until they close the app fully or tap I already paid, and a cancelled or refunded plan stays open until the next fresh start. Buying is not switched on yet, so nobody meets this today.
expected: When Google Play confirms a waiting payment, Plus opens at once, and the app asks Google Play again whenever it comes back to the front.
who: members who buy Plus with a slow payment method, or cancel it
how_often: every waiting payment, once payments are live
fix_line: Pass Google Play's late answers to the app and ask again when the app comes back

title: The free month starts again after the app is removed and installed again
what: The day the free month started is kept only on the phone. Removing the app and installing it again, or clearing its data in Android settings, gives a new free month with every paid feature open. Nothing on the server or in the member's MettleUp account remembers it.
expected: Each person gets one free month, as the help says, kept with their MettleUp account where they have one.
who: people without a gym who know the trick
how_often: whenever someone reinstalls, once the paid plan is switched on
fix_line: Keep the free month's start day with the member's account

title: A yearly Plus buyer on a new phone is told they pay every month
what: Google Play does not say whether a running plan is monthly or yearly, so the app remembers which one this phone bought. On a new phone, or after the app's data is cleared, I already paid finds the plan but the app guesses monthly. The MettleUp Plus page and Settings then say You have MettleUp Plus, paid every month, to someone who paid for a year.
expected: When the app cannot tell, it says the member has MettleUp Plus without naming monthly or yearly.
who: yearly buyers who change phone or clear data
how_often: every restore on a new phone, once payments are live
fix_line: Leave out the month or year words when the app does not know

title: A MettleUp Plus payment that was waiting does not open Plus when Google Play confirms it, until the app is closed and opened again
what: When Google Play answers that a payment is waiting (for example a UPI payment not yet approved), the member reads that Plus opens when Google Play confirms it. When Play later confirms it while the app is still open, the phone takes note of the payment with Google but never tells the app, and the app only asks Google Play again when it is started fresh. So the member has paid and the paid features stay locked until they close the app or tap I already paid.
expected: When Google Play confirms a waiting payment, Plus opens at once (or at least the next time the app comes back to the screen), as the message promised.
who: members who buy MettleUp Plus with a payment Google Play holds as waiting
how_often: not yet (starts the day payments go live); then every waiting payment
fix_line: When Google Play reports a confirmed purchase with no screen waiting, pass it to the app, and ask Google Play again whenever the app comes back to the front

title: MettleUp Plus purchases are kept only on the member's phone, so MettleUp never sees who paid, how much, or a refund
what: A MettleUp Plus purchase through Google Play is noted only in the phone's own storage. No server checks the purchase with Google and nothing is saved where HQ can see it. The phone code itself says server checking comes later, with payments live. So once buying opens, HQ has no list of buyers, no amounts to match against Google Play's payout, no way to see a refund, and a changed copy of the app could open Plus without paying.
expected: Before payments go live, each Plus purchase is checked with Google by the server and kept there, so HQ can see buyers, amounts and refunds and the phone cannot simply claim it paid.
who: MettleUp HQ and the owner, once member payments go live
how_often: not yet (starts the day payments go live); then every purchase
fix_line: Add a server check of each Google Play purchase before the payments-live switch is turned on, and show buyers and refunds in HQ

title: The refunds page says members never pay MettleUp, but the app is ready to sell MettleUp Plus to members, with no refund rule for it
what: The public refunds and cancellation page says members of a gym never pay MettleUp and the member app is free. The member app already holds a paid MettleUp Plus with monthly, yearly and for-life prices bought through Google Play. It is switched off today, so nothing is wrong yet, but the day it is switched on the refunds page becomes untrue and says nothing on how a member cancels or gets money back.
expected: A note on the payments-live switch that the refunds page must change the same day, adding how members cancel and get refunds for MettleUp Plus (through Google Play).
who: members who buy MettleUp Plus, once it is switched on
how_often: not yet (starts the day MettleUp Plus is switched on)
fix_line: Write the member Plus refund and cancel rule into the refunds page, ready for the switch day

title: A member who bought the yearly plan is told they pay every month after moving to a new phone
what: Google Play does not tell the app which plan a subscription is on. When a member taps I already paid on a new phone, or reinstalls, the app guesses monthly, and the top of the Plus screen and Settings then say they pay every month even when they pay yearly.
expected: The line says what the member really pays, or just says they have MettleUp Plus without naming monthly or yearly when it is not known.
who: yearly buyers on a new or reset phone
how_often: not yet (starts the day payments go live)
fix_line: When the plan is not known, show a line without monthly or yearly

title: After the owner changes the gym's UPI ID, members are still shown the old one to pay
what: Each payment asked of a member (a fee, or a shop order) keeps the UPI ID the gym had on the day it was made. When the owner saves a new UPI ID, only the gym's setting changes. A member's open fee and any open shop order keep showing the old QR, the old Pay by UPI app link and the old ID to copy, for up to 30 days, and a shop order reuses that same request each time the member taps pay. Money sent that way goes to an account the gym may no longer use, or to a staff member's old ID.
expected: Every open payment shows the gym's current UPI ID; changing it updates or remakes the open ones.
who: members, owners
how_often: each time a gym changes its UPI ID while payments are open
fix_line: Read the gym's current UPI ID when showing an open payment

title: A shop order paid in the app still says pay at the desk
what: Under every order that is Ordered or Ready the app always writes Pay at the desk when you collect it, or Pay when you collect it. It does not look at whether the order was already paid online. So a paid order shows Paid. The gym can see it. and, on the same card, Pay at the desk. The order placed message and the bag also say pay at the desk and nothing is charged in the app, while the order card offers Pay for this order. With the gym's Shop page also showing the order as unpaid, the member is likely to pay twice.
expected: A paid order says it is paid and drops the pay-at-desk line; the bag and order messages mention that paying in the app is possible when it is on.
who: members
how_often: every shop order paid in the app
fix_line: Hide the pay-at-desk line when the order is paid, and word the bag for both ways

title: After paying for a shop order online, the order still shows the pay buttons
what: When the member comes back from the payment page or a UPI app, the membership fee box asks again and turns to Paid. The shop order does not: My orders only reads the payments when the page is opened, its 10-second refresh reloads orders but not payments, and nothing asks the payment company on return. The card keeps the QR, Pay by UPI app and Pay online until the member leaves and reopens the page, so the member cannot tell it worked and may pay again by UPI.
expected: Coming back to the app re-checks the order's payment and shows Paid at once, as the membership box does.
who: members
how_often: every shop order paid online
fix_line: Re-check an open shop payment when the app comes back to the front

title: When the gym's payment link runs out, the Pay your gym box disappears with no word
what: A fee the desk asked for is shown only while its payment is open or was paid in the last 3 days. Once the payment company says the link ran out, the server marks it ran out and the app's list leaves it out, so the whole Pay your gym box, with the UPI QR that never runs out, vanishes. The words This payment link has run out. Ask the desk for a new one. appear only if the member happens to be on the screen at that moment. The member still owes the money but the app now looks as if nothing is due.
expected: A fee whose link ran out stays listed with the amount, the UPI way to pay, and the line to ask the desk for a new link.
who: members
how_often: each fee link that runs out before the member pays
fix_line: Keep ran-out fees in the member's list with the ask-the-desk line

title: With no internet, Pay for this order says the gym has not set up online payment
what: Tapping Pay for this order with weak or no signal, or when the server is slow, gets no answer. The app reads every missing answer as Online payment is not set up at this gym yet. Pay at the desk., and keeps saying it until the page is opened again, even at a gym where paying online works.
expected: No answer says there is no connection and offers to try again.
who: members
how_often: each pay tap without a working connection
fix_line: Tell a failed call apart from a gym without online payment

title: A fee the gym asked a member to pay quietly disappears from the member app after 7 days, though it is still owed
what: When the desk asks a member to pay a fee and the gym has a payment company connected, the online payment link runs out after 7 days. From then on the member app's list leaves the fee out completely, because it only shows asks that are still open or paid. A fee asked more than 30 days ago is also left out, even one that never runs out. The app has words ready for this case (This payment link has run out. Ask the desk for a new one.) but they never reach the My membership card. The member sees nothing owed and may think the fee is settled.
expected: A fee the member still owes stays on My membership, with a plain line that the payment link ran out and the desk can send a new one.
who: members of gyms that ask for fees in the app
how_often: every fee not paid within 7 days of the ask
fix_line: Keep run-out fee asks in the member's list and show the ready-made run-out words

title: Renew my plan asks the member to pick a plan without showing what any plan costs
what: The Renew my plan list shows each plan's name and length only. The server never sends a price, and the app is written to never show one, on the old reason that the member's number is not checked. The plan prices are the gym's own list, not the member's private data, and the same card already shows the member's dues in rupees when the gym takes payments in the app. A member sends a renewal for a plan without knowing what the desk will charge.
expected: Each plan in the renew list shows its price, so the member knows what they agree to before sending the request.
who: members who renew from the app
how_often: every renewal request
fix_line: Send and show each plan's price in the renew list

title: Renewal and plan-ending words always say pay at the desk, also at gyms that take payments in the member app
what: The renew help says you pay at the desk, an approved renewal says Pay at the desk if you have not yet, and the plan-ending card and Workout tab card say Renew at the desk or front desk. None of these look at the gym's switch for taking payments in the member app. At a gym with that switch on, the same My membership card can show a Pay your gym box with UPI and online buttons right next to words telling the member to pay at the desk.
expected: When the gym takes payments in the app, these lines say the member can pay in the app or at the desk.
who: members of gyms that take payments in the app
how_often: every renewal and plan-ending card at those gyms
fix_line: Pick the pay words from the gym's in-app payment switch

title: When a gym membership ends, the gym's workout plan just says 'No longer sent', with no word on why or that renewing brings it back
what: Workout plans a gym gives to everyone on a membership plan reach the member only while that membership covers today. The day it ends, the folder on the Workout tab changes to 'No longer sent by <gym>'. The same words are used when the trainer withdraws the plan, so the member cannot tell that the membership ending caused it, or that renewing brings it back (it does: renewing updates the folder again).
expected: When the plan stopped because the membership ended, the line says so and points to renewing at the gym.
who: members
how_often: every membership that ends while a plan-wide workout plan is assigned
fix_line: Have the gym's answer say the membership ended, and show 'Your membership ended. Renew at the desk to get this plan again.'

title: A member who buys MettleUp Plus during a workout still gets no suggested weights in that workout
what: Once the paid plan lock is switched on, a free member sees a 'suggestions are part of Plus' line on each exercise and can tap it to buy. The workout remembers its suggestions by the exercises and settings only, not by whether the member may use them. After buying and coming back, the workout thinks it already has its answer (none), so no suggested weight appears, and the locked line also goes away. Suggestions only show once an exercise is added, swapped or a setting changes, or in the next workout. Not live today: the lock is off for everyone.
expected: Right after paying, the open workout shows suggested weights on every exercise.
who: members who buy Plus from inside a workout
how_often: every purchase made during a workout, once the lock is on
fix_line: Make the workout recheck its suggestions when the member's plan changes.

title: When MettleUp Plus starts or stops in the middle of a workout, the watch keeps its old screen until the next set
what: The phone only saves the new watch lock; it does not send the watch a fresh screen. A member who buys Plus during a workout still sees 'Your watch needs MettleUp Plus' (and gets no rest buzz) until the phone next updates the watch. A member whose free month ends during a workout keeps a working watch screen, and the phone still accepts sets logged from it, because the phone never checks the plan when a set comes from the watch.
expected: The moment the plan opens or closes, the watch screen changes to match, and sets from a locked watch are not taken.
who: members with a watch, once Plus is switched on
how_often: only when the plan changes during a workout
fix_line: When the lock changes, resend the current workout and rest to the watch, and ignore watch sets while locked

title: Only Razorpay's open and cancelled answers are ever checked against the real payment company
what: The one cloud check that talks to a real payment company covers Razorpay only, and only a link that is opened and then cancelled, plus wrong keys. Cashfree, PayU and PhonePe, which owners can also connect, are only ever tested against a pretend company, even though two of them take amounts in rupees instead of paise. A paid, expired, failed or refunded answer is never checked against any real company.
expected: Before payments go live, every company an owner can connect is checked in its test mode, including a paid link (amount read back equal to the amount asked) and an expired or refunded one.
who: gym owners and members once payments go live
how_often: every change to payment code
fix_line: Add the same test-mode check for Cashfree, PayU and PhonePe, and cover a paid and an expired link

title: Making the free trial longer for one branch leaves the other branches' trial ending on the old day
what: A business with branches has one free trial: each new branch copies the first branch's trial dates. But when MettleUp HQ makes the trial longer (or shorter), only the one branch it was done on changes. The other branches keep the old end date, so on those branches the owner is told the free trial has ended and is asked to pick a paid plan while the main branch is still free. HQ has no way to do it for the whole business at once.
expected: A change to the trial of a business with branches changes the trial of every branch, or HQ is told which branches still need the same change.
who: owners with more than one branch whose trial HQ changes
how_often: every trial change on a business with branches
fix_line: Apply a trial change to every branch of the same business

title: HQ can cut a new gym's free trial to less than the 3 months the website and terms promise
what: The refund page and the terms say every new gym gets 3 months free. The server lets HQ move a gym's trial end to any moment that is not already past, even one minute from now, as long as a reason is typed. Nothing stops a trial being cut below 3 months from its start.
expected: HQ can make a trial longer, but never end it earlier than 3 months after it started, unless the wording on the website changes.
who: gym owners on the free trial
how_often: only when HQ shortens a trial
fix_line: Refuse a trial end earlier than 3 months after the start, or say on the pages that MettleUp can shorten it

title: A shop order marked Collected by mistake can never be undone, and a returned item cannot be recorded
what: At the desk one tap moves a shop order straight from new to Collected, and the admin app says the money was taken. The server treats Collected as final: there is no way back, no cancel and no return. If the desk taps it by mistake, or the member later returns the item, the order stays Collected, the member's app shows it collected, the stock is not put back and the member's spending total keeps the money.
expected: A Collected order can be taken back by the owner for a short time, and a returned item can be recorded with the money given back and the stock restored.
who: gym owners and desk staff using the shop; members whose order is wrong
how_often: every mis-tap or return
fix_line: Let the owner undo Collected and record a return with stock put back

title: HQ can save a gym's paid plan with a paid-until date that has already passed
what: When HQ sets a monthly or yearly plan by hand after a payment, the server checks that the paid-until date is not more than 3 years ahead, but not that it is in the future. A typo such as last year's date is saved, and the gym that just paid is shown as already run out.
expected: A monthly or yearly plan needs a paid-until date after today.
who: gym owners whose plan HQ sets by hand
how_often: only on an HQ typo
fix_line: Refuse a paid-until date that is not after today

title: The server does not check the price of a shop choice such as a size or flavour
what: A product's own price must be between Rs 1 and Rs 1,00,000 on the server, but a choice (size, flavour) with its own price is saved without any check, and orders are charged at that price. The admin app checks it, so today only an old or broken app could save a choice at Rs 0 or a wrong amount; the member app would then show the product's price while the order is charged the choice's price.
expected: The server checks a choice's own price the same way as the product's price.
who: members ordering from the gym shop
how_often: rare: only if a bad price gets past the admin app
fix_line: Check each choice's price on the server as for the product

title: HQ's count of receipts cancelled this month can include receipts cancelled months ago
what: HQ shows how many receipts a gym cancelled this month. It counts by the last time the receipt row was saved, not by when it was cancelled. Sending the same receipt again (which the server allows, for example when a phone retries) stamps it as saved today, so an old cancelled receipt is counted again this month.
expected: The count uses the day the receipt was cancelled, kept in the receipt history.
who: MettleUp HQ watching for cancelled receipts
how_often: whenever an old cancelled receipt is sent again
fix_line: Count cancels from the receipt history by the cancel time

title: A UPI or bank payment to MettleUp that is confirmed by mistake, bounced or paid back can never be undone or marked refunded
what: A payment the owner reports by UPI or bank transfer can only be waiting, confirmed or refused. Once MettleUp confirms it, the gym's plan and paid-until date move on and there is no way to take that back, mark it paid back, or show the owner that money was returned. A founding gym (Pro for life) can still send a payment that can never be confirmed; the money has arrived but the only choice is to refuse it, with no record that it was sent back. The refunds page promises money back for paying twice or paying too much.
expected: MettleUp can mark a confirmed or refused payment as paid back (with the date and how), and the gym's paid time is put back when a confirmed payment is reversed; a Pro-for-life gym is told it has nothing to pay before it sends money.
who: owners, MettleUp office
how_often: each wrong, bounced or refunded UPI or bank payment
fix_line: Add a paid-back state for UPI and bank payments that also undoes the paid time, and stop a Pro-for-life gym from sending a payment

title: An owner whose number already had a free trial gets a new gym with no free months and is never told
what: Once WhatsApp-checked sign-up is on, a gym made with a number that already started a free trial, or that already owns a gym, is made with its trial ending the moment it is created. The server says so in its answer, but the sign-up screen never reads it and the new-gym screen says nothing about it. The refunds page says every new gym gets 3 months free. With the plan limits switched on, that gym goes to basic mode after 7 days and read-only after 37, with no warning at sign-up.
expected: The sign-up screen tells the owner before and after creating the gym that this number has already used its free months and what it costs to carry on; the refunds page says one free trial per number.
who: owners opening a second gym or signing up again
how_often: every sign-up with a used number, once the number check is on
fix_line: Show the no-free-trial answer on sign-up and make the refunds page say one trial per number

title: Once a gym is read-only for not paying MettleUp, money the desk already took and printed a receipt for cannot be saved
what: When the plan limits are on and a gym has been unpaid for more than 37 days, the server refuses every desk record, receipts included. A receipt printed at a desk with no internet was promised never to be refused, but it now stays stuck on that device. Members who paid the gym also cannot be checked in, so an entry machine turns them away. The refunds page says the gym can still look and export, but not that cash already taken cannot be recorded.
expected: Receipts for money already taken (at least offline ones) and member check-ins are still saved in read-only, or the owner is warned clearly before read-only starts that the desk will stop recording fees and entries.
who: desks and members of a gym that stopped paying
how_often: every receipt and check-in after day 37 unpaid, once the switch is on
fix_line: Let receipts and check-ins through in read-only, or warn the owner plainly before it starts

title: In test mode, a real gym owner who pays with a test card gets a real paid plan and a real receipt
what: Buying a MettleUp plan online only works with the payment company's test keys today. But the payment it takes is treated like real money: the gym's paid-until date moves on, the plan changes, and a numbered MettleUp receipt is made. The owner's billing screen and receipt never say test mode. The switch that opens Pay online is one switch for every gym, so turning it on to try it with the test gym opens it for every gym, and any owner could get a year of Pro with a test card.
expected: While payments are in test mode, a test payment should not give a real gym real paid time or a real receipt number, and the owner's screen should say test mode; or Pay online should open only for the test gym.
who: MettleUp
how_often: only if the Pay online switch is turned on while payments are in test mode
fix_line: Mark test payments as test (no paid time, no numbered receipt), or open Pay online per gym for testing

title: An owner whose payment could not become a plan is told nothing
what: When the payment company takes the owner's money but it cannot become a plan (the amount was not what was asked, or the gym changed in between, for example it went Pro for life on another link), the money is kept for MettleUp to refund or set by hand. The owner's billing screen still shows the old plan and end date, no receipt, and no word that the payment arrived and is being checked. Only the MettleUp office list shows it.
expected: The owner's billing screen should say that a payment arrived, that it could not be applied yet, that MettleUp will refund it or set the plan, and what happened once it is done.
who: owners
how_often: rare: only when a paid link cannot be applied
fix_line: Show held payments and their outcome on the owner's billing screen

title: Moving from Starter up to Pro costs more than the price difference
what: The move-up price is the monthly difference divided by 30 (or the yearly one by 365), times the days left counting today. A paid month runs from today to the same date next month, which is 31 days counted that way (a year is 366). So an owner who pays Starter monthly and moves up the same day pays Rs 517, not Rs 500, and Rs 1,516 in all, more than Pro's Rs 1,499. On yearly the move-up is Rs 5,013, not Rs 4,999. The refund page says you pay only the difference for the days left.
expected: Moving up should never cost more than the price difference, and Starter plus a move-up should never cost more than buying Pro.
who: owners
how_often: every move-up
fix_line: Cap the move-up at the full price difference, or count the days the same way the paid month does

title: Test-mode payments are announced to members and gyms as real
what: Member payment requests and payments made while payments are still in test mode (no real money) go out like real ones. A member gets a phone pop-up saying their gym asked them to pay their fee, tap to pay. The gym's alert bell says the member paid online, see it on Money. Neither says test mode, though each payment request knows whether it was test or live.
expected: A test-mode request should not pop up on a real member's phone, and a test-mode payment's alert should say it was a test with no real money.
who: members and owners
how_often: every payment request or payment while payments are in test mode
fix_line: Pass test or live with each request and skip the member pop-up, or say test, for test ones

title: While payments are in test mode, the member app shows a test payment as paid, but the gym records nothing
what: Payments are in test mode for every gym today, yet any gym that connects Razorpay or Cashfree has the member app pay switch on by default. Members then get test payment pages for their dues and shop orders. A member who finishes one sees Paid, thank you (or Paid. The gym can see it. for a shop order), while no money moved, the gym's Shop page does not show the order as paid and the due stays open at the desk. The join page and the gym web page are kept away from test payments on purpose; the member app is not.
expected: Real members are never shown a test payment page. In test mode the member app shows the UPI QR or says pay at the desk, the same rule as the join page.
who: members of gyms that connected a payment company
how_often: every member payment while payments are in test mode
fix_line: Offer company links in the member app only when payments are live, as the join page does

title: A gym still on its trial can be told the AI Assistant is resting for the month although it has AI credits
what: The AI Assistant counts a gym as paying only when its MettleUp plan is paid. All trial and unpaid gyms share one small monthly spending cap. Once those gyms together reach it, every one of them is told the assistant is resting till next month, even a gym that holds AI credits MettleUp added for it. The credits are taken only after this check, so they sit unused.
expected: A gym with AI credits can use them; the shared trial cap applies only to free use.
who: owners of gyms in their trial
how_often: once the shared monthly cap is used up
fix_line: Skip the shared trial cap for a gym whose credit balance is above zero

title: The refunds page says AI credits for a failed task come back automatically, but they are asked back only once and can be lost
what: The refunds page promises that if an AI task fails after its credits are taken, the same credits come back automatically. The admin app asks for them back once, straight after the failure. If that one ask fails (often the same lost internet that made the task fail), nothing tries again, and after 10 minutes the server refuses any give-back. The owner silently loses the credits.
expected: Credits for a failed task always come back, even when the internet drops at that moment, or the page does not promise it.
who: owners
how_often: sometimes, when a task fails with a bad connection
fix_line: Retry the give-back later, or let the server give it back itself when a task is marked failed

title: The About page says free credits end at the end of each month, but the 20 starter credits never end
what: The About page lists 20 free credits for the free trial, then says free credits end on the last day of each month. The server never takes the 20 starter credits back: only the monthly free credits of yearly and founding gyms run out. An owner reading the page may rush to use credits that in fact stay.
expected: The page says the 20 starter credits stay until used, or the server ends them the way the page says.
who: owners
how_often: every reader of the About page
fix_line: Say on the page that the 20 starter credits do not end at month end

title: After a test-mode payment the join page just says Paid with the amount, with no word that no real money moved
what: While the gym's online payments are in test mode, the join page shows a test-mode note before paying. Once the test payment goes through, the page says Paid and the amount and that the gym will approve the request, and the test-mode note is no longer shown.
expected: The paid line also says it was a test payment and no real money moved.
who: gym owners trying payments, and anyone who joins while the gym tests
how_often: every test payment on the join page
fix_line: Keep the test-mode note under the paid line

title: The gym's web page rounds plan prices to whole rupees, while the join page charges the exact price
what: The admin app lets a gym set a plan price with paise, such as 1,499.50. The gym's own web page rounds every price and joining fee to whole rupees, so it shows 1,500. The join page reached from the same button shows and charges 1,499.50.
expected: Both pages show the same amount the member will pay.
who: people looking at a gym's web page
how_often: only for prices with paise
fix_line: Show paise on the gym page the same way as on the join page
